contractual obligation,coverage	Insurer
Life Assurance
The insurer provides life assurance coverage and is bound to pay the sum assured, but is not entitled to subrogation against persons causing the insured event.

legal requirement,residence	Egypt
Suretyship
Suretyship provisions require the surety to be a solvent person residing in Egypt, or alternatively the debtor may provide adequate real security.

document surrender,guarantee,guarantee enforcement,legal proceedings,security,security transfer,undertaking	Creditor
Surety
The Surety guarantees the debt to the Creditor and is released when the Debtor's tender is accepted or declared valid and the Debtor retracts with the Creditor's acceptance.<SEP>The surety undertakes to the creditor to fulfil the debtor's obligation if the debtor fails to do so, and the creditor must first proceed against the debtor before pursuing the surety.<SEP>The creditor may only take proceedings against the surety after first proceeding against the debtor and exhausting the debtor's property, unless the surety is jointly and severally liable.<SEP>The creditor is bound to hand over to the surety all documents necessary for the right of action upon discharge of the debt, and must comply with formalities for transferring any immovable property security.

contractual obligation,liability	Fire Insurance
Insurer
The insurer under fire insurance is liable for all fire-related damage including salvage measures damage, loss during fire, and damage from defects in the insured thing, and is entitled to subrogation against the author of the damaging act.

age limit,validity	Life Assurance
Table of Rates
Life assurance may be rendered void if the true age of the life assured exceeds the limit specified in the table of rates.

civil act,classification	Commercial Debt
Suretyship
Suretyship entered into in respect of a commercial debt is deemed a civil act even if the surety is a trader, except for guarantees arising from negotiable instruments.

discharge,forfeiture of rights,guarantee,notice requirement	Debtor
Surety
The surety guarantees the debtor's obligation, is discharged simultaneously with the debtor, and may revoke the guarantee for future debts if no duration was fixed and the debt has not yet been created.<SEP>A surety must notify the debtor before paying the debt; failure to do so results in forfeiture of the surety's right of action against the debtor if the debtor has already paid or has grounds to have the debt declared void or extinguished.

compensation,coverage	Insured
Insurer
The insurer is liable to compensate the insured for covered events, including unintentional fault and force majeure, but not for deliberate or fraudulent damage caused by the insured.

entitlement,protection	Beneficiary
Life Assurance
The beneficiary is designated to receive the sum assured under life assurance, and the insurer cannot be subrogated to the beneficiary's rights against persons causing the insured event.

commercial classification,exception	Commercial Debt
Negotiable Instruments
Suretyship resulting from backing signatures or endorsements on negotiable instruments is always deemed a commercial act, creating an exception to the general rule that suretyship for a commercial debt is a civil act.

contractual role,obligation	Surety
Suretyship
The surety is the central party in the suretyship contract, bound to perform the obligation if the debtor defaults, and must be solvent and reside in Egypt.

adjustment,payment	Insurer
Sum Assured
The insurer is obligated to pay the sum assured, which may be reduced proportionally if the agreed premium was lower than the correct premium based on the true age of the life assured.

payment obligation	Insured
Premium
The insured is responsible for paying the agreed premium, and incorrect particulars affecting the premium result in proportional adjustments to the sum assured.

exception,liability limitation	Fire Insurance
Theft
The insurer under fire insurance is not liable for loss or disappearance of insured things during a fire if the insurer can establish that the loss was caused by theft.

guarantee limit,revocation	Future Debt
Surety
The surety may enter into a guarantee for a future debt if the amount is fixed beforehand, and may revoke the guarantee at any time if no duration was fixed and the guaranteed debt has not yet been created.

custody,deposit,expenses,indemnification,obligation,remuneration	Depositor
Depository
The Depositor must pay agreed remuneration upon termination of the deposit and reimburse the Depository for preservation expenses and indemnify against losses resulting from the deposit.<SEP>The Depositor entrusts property to the Depository for safekeeping under a deposit contract, and the Depository must safeguard and return the thing deposited.

legal right,limitation	Insurer
Subrogation
The insurer has the right of subrogation in fire insurance to pursue claims against third parties causing the damage, but this right does not apply in life assurance.

compensation transfer,security	Insured
Pledge
When the insured thing is encumbered with a pledge, the rights under the pledge transfer to the insurance compensation due to the debtor.

compensation,liability,sale	Heir of Depository
Owner
The Heir of Depository who sells the deposited thing in good faith is liable to refund the price received or assign rights against the Purchaser to the Owner.

coverage extension,default scope	Accessories of Debt
Surety
In the absence of an express agreement, suretyship extends to the accessories of the debt, including expenses of the first demand for payment and expenses incurred after notice to the surety.

debt,hotel charges,liability,limitation,notice,prescription,privilege over effects,safekeeping,service relationship,time limit	Hotel Proprietor
Traveller
Hotel Proprietors are responsible for safeguarding the effects brought by Travellers, with liability limited to L.E. 50 for valuables unless gross negligence or refusal to accept custody is proven.<SEP>The Traveller must inform the Hotel Proprietor of theft, loss, or damage without delay, and legal action prescribes six months after leaving the establishment.<SEP>The Hotel Proprietor has a privilege over the Traveller's effects brought into the hotel for unpaid accommodation, provisions, and expenses, as established in Article 1144.<SEP>The hotel proprietor is owed sums by the traveller for accommodation, food, and expenses incurred on the traveller's account.

accountability,management,safeguarding	Judicial Custody
Receiver
The Receiver is entrusted under Judicial Custody to preserve, manage, and return property subject to litigation, keeping regular accounts and rendering annual reports.

legal notification,payment restriction	Insurer
Judicial Deposit
When the insured thing has been placed under judicial deposit and the insurer is duly notified, the insurer is prohibited from paying any sum due to the insured.

compensation transfer,security	Insured
Mortgage
When the insured thing is encumbered with a mortgage, the rights under the mortgage transfer to the insurance compensation due to the debtor.

restitution,return	Depository
Owner
The Depository is bound to return the deposited thing to the Owner upon demand, unless the deposit term was fixed for the Depository's benefit.

alienation,sale	Heir of Depository
Purchaser
The Heir of Depository may sell the deposited thing to the Purchaser in good faith, creating rights that may be assigned to the Owner.

annuity payment,contract,contractual breach,obligation,remedies	Beneficiary
Grantor
If the Grantor fails to fulfil his obligation, the Beneficiary may demand due performance of the contract or, if the contract is for valuable consideration, apply for its resiliation together with damages.<SEP>The Grantor is obligated to pay periodic Life Annuity payments to the Beneficiary, and failure to perform entitles the Beneficiary to demand performance or contract resiliation.

authorization,consumable goods,conversion	Contract of Loan for Consumption
Deposit
A Deposit converts into a Contract of Loan for Consumption when the deposited object is consumable and the Depository is authorized to use it.

appointment,authority,oversight	Judge
Receiver
The Judge appoints the Receiver when interested parties cannot agree, and may order the Receiver's books to be stamped by the Court.

administration,judicial order,protection	Judicial Custody
Wakf Property
Judicial Custody may be ordered over Wakf Property when the Nazir's office is vacant, disputed, or subject to removal, or when the Wakf is indebted or a beneficiary is insolvent.

coverage,liability	Force Majeure
Insured
The insured is covered for damage resulting from fortuitous events of force majeure, for which the insurer is held liable.

negligence,vicarious liability	Hotel Proprietor
Hotel Staff
The Hotel Proprietor bears full liability for loss or damage caused by the gross negligence of Hotel Staff, removing the L.E. 50 limitation on compensation.

rights protection,wrongful administration	Creditors
Nazir
Creditors' rights against the Wakf are safeguarded through judicial custody when threatened by the Nazir's wrongful administration or bad faith.

accountability,consent,reporting	Interested Parties
Receiver
The Receiver must render annual accounts of receipts and expenditure to Interested Parties, may not appoint one of them as substitute without the others' consent, and must not perform non-administrative acts without their unanimous consent.

enforcement,exception,voidability	Gaming and Betting
Judge
Gaming and Betting agreements are void, but the Judge has authority to reduce excessive stakes in sports bets and to allow exceptions for legally authorized lotteries.

creation,testamentary disposition	Life Annuity
Will
A Life Annuity obligation may be created by Will as an alternative to creation by contract, allowing testamentary establishment of periodic payment commitments.

damage coverage,protective action	Insured
Salvage Measures
Damage caused to insured things by salvage measures taken during a fire is included in the insurer's liability to the insured.

applicable rules,legal hierarchy	Right of User and Occupation
Usufruct
The rules governing usufruct apply to the Right of User and Occupation provided they are not incompatible with the nature of these two rights.

administration,leasing authority,management	Nazir
Wakf Property
The Nazir has the exclusive authority to administer, lease, and collect rent for wakf property.<SEP>The Nazir is the administrator of wakf property and is authorized to lease it, subject to the three-year limit without judicial authorization.<SEP>The Nazir is responsible for administering and managing the Wakf Property, and the quality of that administration determines whether judicial custody is imposed.

legal dependency,property requirement	Hekr
Wakf
Hekr may only be established on land that is constituted in wakf, and hekr rights are affected by changes in wakf status of the land.

category,inclusion	Aleatory Contracts
Gaming and Betting
Gaming and Betting is a subcategory of Aleatory Contracts, governed as Section I of Chapter IV.

Grantor of Hekr
The grantee of the hekr must pay the agreed rent to the grantor, and the grantor may demand resiliation if rent is unpaid for three consecutive years.

form requirements,gratuitous settlement	Contract of Gift
Life Annuity
A Life Annuity settled gratuitously must satisfy both the writing requirement and the special formal requirements applicable to Contracts of Gift under the law.

oversight,removal,vacancy	Judicial Custody
Nazir
Judicial Custody may be triggered by the vacancy of the Nazir, litigation between co-nazirs, removal proceedings, or wrongful administration by the Nazir, and ends upon appointment of a new Nazir.

contracting party,property management	Idjaratein
Wakf
Idjaratein is a contract by which a wakf creates a hekr on land containing buildings in need of repair.

judicial oversight,legal authorization	Charie Court of First Instance
Hekr
Hekr requires the permission of the Charie Court of First Instance and must be formalized by a deed drawn up by the President of the Court or a delegated official.

legal framework,property rights	Servitudes
Usufruct
Both servitudes and usufruct are property rights within the same legal code that limit or govern the use of real property.

category,inclusion	Aleatory Contracts
Life Annuity
Life Annuity is a subcategory of Aleatory Contracts, governed as Section II of Chapter IV.

lease agreement,property management	Kholou-el-intifaa
Wakf
Kholou-el-intifaa is a lease contract granted by a wakf for an indefinite period, which the wakf may resiliate at any time with due notice and compensation.

contract subtype,legal applicability	Hekr
Idjaratein
Idjaratein is a specific type of hekr contract and is subject to the rules governing hekr, with modifications specified in its defining provision.

legal entitlement,rights holder	Usufruct
Usufructuary
The usufructuary is the holder of the usufruct right, which terminates upon the usufructuary's death and is subject to the conditions of the creating deed.

creation of rights,property division	Original Owner
Servitudes
Apparent servitudes may be created by the intention of the original owner when establishing an apparent distinction between two separate properties.

court authorization,legal procedure	Article 1000
Charie Court of First Instance
Article 1000 requires permission from the Charie Court of First Instance for the establishment of hekr.

category,inclusion	Aleatory Contracts
Contract of Insurance
Contract of Insurance is a subcategory of Aleatory Contracts, governed as Section III of Chapter IV.

delegation,official duty	Judge
President of the Court
A Judge may be delegated by the President of the Court to draw up the hekr deed.

legal governance,termination rules	Article 1008
Hekr
Article 1008 governs the conditions under which the right of hekr terminates, including at the end of the fixed period or upon specific events.

legal governance,termination rules	Article 993
Usufruct
Article 993 governs the termination of usufruct and provisions regarding standing crops upon termination or death of the usufructuary.

legal limitation,property rights	Servitudes
State Property
A servitude may be imposed on State property provided it is not incompatible with the use for which the property is intended.

Law Relating to the Publication of Real Rights

delegation,official duty	Notary
President of the Court

establishment,revocation rights	Founder of Wakf

The grantee of the hekr holds the right to dispose of it, owns constructions and plantations absolutely, and must maintain the land for exploitation.

Usufruct
Article 994 governs the extinction of usufruct through loss of property and its transmission to substitute property.

Apparent servitudes are a subcategory of servitudes that may be created by the intention of the original owner and are the only servitudes acquirable by prescription.

delegation,judicial authority	Charie Court of First Instance
President of the Court
The President of the Court is the official at the Charie Court of First Instance who draws up the hekr deed or delegates this task.

contract,employment,obligations	Master (رب العمل)
Worker (العامل)
The Worker is employed by the Master under a contract of service, with both parties having reciprocal rights and obligations including performance of work, payment of salary, obedience of orders, and duty of care.

building restrictions,legal governance	Article 1018
Servitudes
Article 1018 provides that building restrictions imposed on a property constitute servitude rights for the benefit of other properties.

legal classification,property rights	Apparent Servitudes
Rights of Way
Rights of way are a type of apparent servitude that can be acquired by prescription.

employment,legal obligations	Contract of Service
Worker (العامل)
The Worker is bound by the Contract of Service to personally perform work, obey orders, preserve entrusted items, and safeguard trade secrets.

Insolvency

legal provision,penal consequences	Article 260
Misappropriation
Article 260 defines the two cases in which a debtor is liable to penalties for misappropriation related to insolvency.

cross-reference,legal provision	Article 261

Article 261 references Article 263 regarding the restoration of original payment terms for debts after insolvency ceases.

lawful withholding,security rights	Possessor
Right of Retention
The possessor may exercise the right of retention over a thing on which necessary or useful expenditure has been incurred, refusing to return it until repayment.

binding effect,successor rights	Hidden Contract
Universal Successors in Title
The hidden (genuine) contract binds universal successors in title together with the original contracting parties.

The President of the Court has the power to grant an alimentary allowance to the debtor upon application when creditor revenues have been attached.

debt obligation,debt relationship,default,financial obligation,financial relationship,judgment,judicial protection,legal entitlement,legal proceedings,legal rights,obligation,payment,proceedings,security	Creditor
Debtor
The (Creditor, Debtor) relation describes the fundamental legal and financial relationship in which a Debtor owes an obligation or debt to a Creditor, who is entitled to receive payment or performance from the Debtor. The Debtor is obligated to fulfill the debt to the Creditor or the Creditor's representative, and this relationship is governed by rules on enforceability, restitution, and premature payment. The Creditor may refuse performance by a person other than the Debtor when the contract or the nature of the obligation requires personal performance.

The Creditor possesses a broad range of rights and remedies to protect and enforce the obligation. The Creditor may take protective measures, demand security, and initiate legal proceedings against the Debtor to recover the debt. Through an enforceable judgment, the Creditor may obtain judgment charges on the Debtor's immovable property, and both parties hold mutual rights to appeal orders related to such judgment charges before the Court of First Instance. The Creditor may also apply for judicial custody of the Debtor's movables charged with a privilege when there are reasonable grounds to fear misappropriation, as provided under Article 1133. When a surety is involved, the Creditor must first take proceedings against the Debtor before pursuing the surety and must prove the debt in bankruptcy to preserve rights against the surety.

On the Debtor's side, the Debtor must provide any promised securities to the Creditor and may be compelled to redeem an annuity upon failure to pay for two consecutive years or upon insolvency. The Debtor may also be subject to insolvency proceedings initiated by the Creditor. However, the Debtor retains certain rights, including the ability to interrupt the running of prescription by expressly or tacitly acknowledging the debt.

When a debtor undertakes to offer a surety, the debtor may alternatively provide adequate real security instead of producing a solvent surety.

validity requirement,void contract	Consideration

Ratification

invalidation,legal principle	Contract
Public Policy
A contract is void if its object or consideration is contrary to public policy.

obligation enforcement,security rights	Debtor
Right of Retention
The right of retention allows withholding performance from a debtor who has not fulfilled connected obligations or provided adequate security.

administrative duty,court officer	Court of First Instance
Greffier
The greffier serves as the registrar of the Court of First Instance, responsible for registering insolvency suits and recording judgments.

error,grounds for avoidance	Avoidance
Mistake
Mistake serves as grounds for avoidance of a contract, with a three-year prescription period from the date of discovery.

court-ordered,judicial authority	Court
Nullity
The court may order nullity on its own initiative when a contract is void.

invalidation,legal standard	Contract
Morality
A contract is void if its object or consideration is contrary to morality.

fraudulent conduct,penal offense	Debtor

judicial review,modification	Contract of Adhesion
Judge
The judge may modify leonine conditions or relieve the adhering party of the obligation to perform them in a contract of adhesion.

jurisdiction,legal provision	Article 250
Court of First Instance

deception,grounds for avoidance	Avoidance
Fraudulent Misrepresentation

confers rights,direct claim	Beneficiary
Stipulation for Third Party

honesty,performance standard	Contract

asset distribution,financial depository	Caisse du Tribunal
Debtor
The Caisse du Tribunal holds the proceeds from debtor property dispositions at normal price for distribution to creditors.

oppressive conditions,unfair terms	Contract of Adhesion
Leonine Condition
Leonine conditions are unfair or oppressive terms found in contracts of adhesion that may be modified by the judge in accordance with equity.

coercion,grounds for avoidance	Avoidance
Duress
Duress serves as grounds for avoidance of a contract, with a three-year prescription period from the date the duress ceases.

creates benefit,revocation,revocation right,stipulation,substitution	Beneficiary
Stipulator
The stipulator may revoke the stipulation in favor of the beneficiary before the beneficiary claims the benefit, substitute a new beneficiary, or retain the benefit for himself.<SEP>The stipulator stipulates an obligation for the benefit of a third party and may revoke the stipulation before the beneficiary accepts it.

non-binding obligations,rights creation	Contract
Third Party
A contract does not create obligations binding upon third parties but may create rights in their favor.

debtor relief,living expenses	Alimentary Allowance
Debtor
The alimentary allowance is a payment granted to the debtor from attached revenues to cover living expenses during insolvency.

creditor payment,financial depository	Caisse du Tribunal
Creditor
The Caisse du Tribunal serves as the depository for funds to be distributed to creditors in accordance with the procedure for distribution.

capacity,grounds for avoidance	Avoidance
Legal Incapacity
Legal incapacity is a ground for avoidance of a contract, with the prescription period running from the date of cessation of such incapacity.

alternative remedy,compensation	Damages
Reinstatement
When reinstatement of parties to their pre-contract position is impossible after a contract is void or annulled, damages equivalent to the loss may be awarded as an alternative remedy.

stipulation,undertaking	Promisor
Stipulator
The promisor undertakes to perform the obligation that the stipulator has stipulated for the benefit of a third party, and the revocation of the stipulation does not automatically liberate the promisor vis-a-vis the stipulator.

rights transfer,succession	Contract
Universal Successor in Title
The effects of a contract apply to the parties and their universal successors in title, subject to the rules relating to successions.

hardship relief,judicial oversight,legal determination,obligation reduction	Debtor
Judge
The judge may reduce the debtor's excessively onerous contractual obligations when exceptional and unpredictable events make performance threaten the debtor with exorbitant loss.<SEP>The judge fixes reasonable times for the debtor's performance, determines the object of obligations when the debtor fails to elect, and adjudicates disputes between debtor and creditor.

debtor relief,legal provision	Alimentary Allowance
Article 259
Article 259 authorizes the President of the Court to grant an alimentary allowance to the debtor from attached revenues.

fairness,modification standard	Contract of Adhesion
Equity
Leonine conditions in a contract of adhesion may be modified by the judge or the adhering party may be relieved of them in accordance with the principles of equity.

fund deposit,legal provision	Article 258
Caisse du Tribunal
Article 258 requires the purchaser to deposit the normal price at the Caisse du Tribunal for distribution among creditors.

legal concept,liability structure	Joint and Several Liability
Suretyship
Joint and several liability applies to sureties either when stipulated in the contract or by operation of law in judicial and legal suretyship, eliminating the surety's right to demand distrainment of the debtor's property first.

contract invalidation,legal distinction	Avoidance
Nullity
Avoidance applies to voidable contracts through a designated party's right, while nullity applies to void contracts and may be invoked by any interested person or ordered by the court.

exclusive control,legal right	Property Owner
Right of Ownership
The right of ownership grants the property owner exclusive rights to use, enjoy, and dispose of property within the limits of the law, including all fruits, products, and accessories.

defenses,obligation performance	Beneficiary
Promisor
The promisor undertakes to perform an obligation for the benefit of the beneficiary and may set up against the beneficiary the defenses arising out of the contract.

obligations,property transfer	Contract
Particular Successor in Title
Obligations and personal rights created by contracts relating to property are transferred to particular successors together with the property when they constitute essential elements.

doubt resolution,favorable construction	Contract Interpretation
Debtor
In cases of doubt during contract interpretation, the construction shall be in favor of the debtor.

debt recovery,legal right	Subrogation
Surety
A surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all of the creditor's rights against the debtor; if only part of the debt is paid, subrogation applies only after the creditor has recovered the full amount from the debtor.

debt guarantee,priority of execution	Real Security
Suretyship
When both real security and suretyship exist for the same debt, the real security must be realized before the surety's property can be seized.

nuisance,property rights,shared obligations	Neighbor
Property Owner
A property owner must not exercise rights excessively to the detriment of a neighbor, and both share obligations for boundary demarcation and may share canal and drainage costs.

access easement,landlocked property	Public Road
Right of Way
An owner whose land is cut off from or lacks adequate access to a public road is entitled to a right of way over neighboring land, subject to fair compensation and the condition of least possible damage.

fairness,performance standard	Contract
Equity
A contract binds the contracting parties not only to its expressed conditions but also to everything which, according to law, usage, and equity, is deemed a necessary sequel to the contract.

contract,obligation,revocation	Debtor
Stipulator
Revocation of a third-party stipulation does not liberate the debtor vis-a-vis the stipulator unless there is an express or implied agreement to the contrary.

guarantee of surety,secondary liability	Sub-Surety
Surety
A sub-surety guarantees the principal surety's obligation, and the creditor may not proceed against the sub-surety before taking action against the principal surety unless both are jointly and severally liable.

correlative obligations,dissolution,non-performance	Bilateral Contract
Rescission
In bilateral contracts, if one party fails to perform his obligation, the other party may demand rescission after serving a formal summons; correlative obligations are extinguished upon impossibility of performance.

ownership extent,surface and subsurface rights	Land
Property Owner
A property owner's ownership of land extends to everything above and below the surface as far as it can be usefully enjoyed, and the surface ownership may be separated from what is above or below by law or agreement.

compensation,legal easement	Neighbor
Right of Way
An owner whose land is cut off from a public road has a right of way over neighboring land, provided fair compensation is paid and the passage causes the least possible damage.

construction,intention ascertainment	Contract
Contract Interpretation
Contract interpretation is the process of ascertaining the common intention of the parties when the contract wording requires construction, going beyond the literal meaning of the words.

claim,injury,prescriptive period	Unlawful Act
Victim
The victim suffers injury from an unlawful act and may claim damages within three years of knowing the injury and the responsible person, or fifteen years from the act.

payment,recovery,subrogation	Debt
Surety
A surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all of the creditor's rights against the debtor and may recover the capital, interest, and expenses from the debtor.

discretion,grace period,judicial authority	Judge
Rescission
The judge may grant additional time to the debtor, reject rescission when the unperformed part is of little importance, or award damages upon rescission.

deprivation of property,just compensation	Fair Compensation
Property Owner
No property owner may be deprived of property except in cases provided by law and upon payment of fair compensation.

damage compensation,water passage	Land
Private Canal or Drain
When damage is caused to land by a canal or drain crossing it, the landowner has the right to claim adequate compensation for the damage done.

employment,supervision,vicarious liability	Master
Servant
The master is liable for damage caused by the servant's unlawful acts performed in the course of or as a result of employment, based on the master's actual powers of supervision and control.

duty of care,supervision,vicarious liability	Minor
Supervisor
The supervisor is liable for injuries caused by the minor's unlawful acts; supervision of a minor transfers to schoolteachers or craft supervisors while under their care.

binding effect,mutual obligation	Contract
Contracting Party
The effects of a contract apply to the contracting parties, binding them to its contents and to everything deemed a necessary sequel according to law, usage, and equity.

custody,harm,strict liability	Animal
Animal Keeper
The animal keeper is strictly liable for harm caused by the animal even if it strays or escapes, unless the harm resulted from a cause beyond the keeper's control.

beyond control,exemption,liability defense	Force Majeure
Unlawful Act
Force majeure and other causes beyond a person's control, such as unforeseen circumstances or the fault of the victim or a third party, exempt that person from liability for injury.

debt recovery,legal proceedings	Creditor
Debt
The creditor holds the right to recover the debt through legal proceedings against the debtor and, under certain conditions, against the surety.

assessment,compensation method,judicial authority,judicial discretion	Damages
Judge
The judge determines the extent of damages in light of circumstances and may order payment by installments, periodical payments, restoration of the original position, or performance of a specific act.<SEP>The judge fixes the amount of damages if not predetermined in a contract or by law, taking into account the prejudice suffered by the creditor and the unjustifiable attitude of the debtor.

cost contribution,shared usage	Neighbor
Private Canal or Drain
Neighboring owners may use a private canal or drain for irrigation or drainage after the owner has satisfied their own needs, and must contribute to construction and maintenance costs in proportion to the benefiting land area.

claim for compensation,recourse,vicarious liability	Right of Redress
Supervisor
A supervisor held liable for the unlawful act of a supervised person has a right of redress against that person to the extent of their responsibility for the injury.

contract type,correlative obligations,synallagmatic	Bilateral Contract
Contract
A bilateral contract is a specific type of contract in which both parties are bound by correlative obligations, and the non-performance by one party may justify the other party's abstention from performance.

authorization,legal requirement	Mandatary (الوكيل)
Special Mandate
A special mandate is required for the mandatary to perform acts beyond management, such as sale, mortgage, gifts, compromise, arbitration, and court representation.

exemption,justification,proportionality	Legitimate Defense
Unlawful Act
Causing injury in legitimate defense of one's person or property exempts the person from liability, provided the defensive measures do not exceed what is necessary.

consent,interest,protection	Mandator (الموكل)
Third Party (الغير)
When a mandate is granted in the interest of a third party, the mandator cannot revoke or restrict it without the third party's consent.

claim for compensation,recourse,vicarious liability	Master
Right of Redress
A master held liable for the unlawful act of a servant has a right of redress against the servant to the extent of the servant's responsibility for the injury.

contractual obligation,custody,return	Depositor (المودع)
Depository (المودع عنده)
The depository receives a thing from the depositor for safe custody and must return it upon request, with varying standards of care depending on whether the deposit is gratuitous or remunerated.

delegation,liability	Mandatary (الوكيل)
Substitute (نائب الوكيل)
The mandatary may nominate a substitute to perform the mandate; liability depends on whether delegation was authorized, with unauthorized delegation making the mandatary fully liable.

immunity,lawful belief,superior orders	Public Official
Unlawful Act
A public official is exempt from liability for an unlawful act causing injury if performed under a superior's obligatory order with reasonable belief in its lawfulness and due care.

judicial oversight,remuneration assessment	Judge (القاضى)
Mandator (الموكل)
The agreed remuneration for a mandate is subject to assessment by the Judge, unless it has been voluntarily paid after performance.

contractual duty,safekeeping	Deposit (الوديعة)
Depository (المودع عنده)
The depository is bound by the deposit contract to take delivery of the thing, keep it in safe custody, and return it in kind.

legal dealings,representation	Mandatary (الوكيل)
Third Party (الغير)
The mandatary deals with third parties on behalf of the mandator, and the relationship is governed by Articles 104 to 107 on representation.

liability,reparation,tort,void clause	Damages
Unlawful Act
Every unlawful act causing injury imposes an obligation to make reparation through damages upon the person who committed it.<SEP>Any contractual clause discharging a person from responsibility for unlawful acts is void, and formal summons is not required when damages arise from an unlawful act.

legal framework,representation	Articles 104 to 107
Mandator (الموكل)
Articles 104 to 107 regarding representation apply to the legal relationship between the mandator and third parties dealing with the mandatary.

duty of diligence,standard of care	Depository (المودع عنده)
Reasonable Person (الرجل المعتاد)
In a remunerated deposit, the depository must exercise the diligence of a reasonable person in the custody of the deposited thing; in a gratuitous deposit, the standard is the care given to own affairs without exceeding the reasonable person threshold.

post-mortem obligation,succession	Heirs (ورثة)
Mandatary (الوكيل)
Upon the death of the mandatary, the heirs are obligated to inform the mandator and take protective measures if they have legal capacity and knowledge of the mandate.

burden and benefit,servitude,subordination	Dominant Tenement
Servient Tenement
The dominant tenement benefits from a servitude that imposes a burden on the servient tenement, creating a legally recognized relationship of subordination between the two properties.

civil action,criminal proceedings,prescription	Damages
Penal Offence
When a damages claim arises from a penal offence, the civil action for damages is only prescribed when the penal action itself is prescribed.

indemnification,restriction,termination	Mandator (الموكل)
Revocation of Mandate
The mandator may revoke or restrict the mandate at any time regardless of contrary agreement, but must indemnify the mandatary for loss from untimely or unjustified revocation of a remunerated mandate, and cannot revoke a mandate in the interest of a third party without consent.

constitution,encumbrance,real right	Immovable Property
Mortgage
A mortgage can only be constituted on immovable property that is marketable, capable of being sold by public auction, and specifically described.

collective responsibility,multiple agents	Joint and Several Liability (التضامن)
Mandatary (الوكيل)
When several mandataries are appointed by the same document without authorization to act severally, they must act jointly and are jointly and severally liable if the mandate is indivisible or if damage sustained by the mandator results from their common fault.

burden,obligation,restriction	Servient Tenement
Servitude
A servitude imposes restrictions and obligations on the servient tenement, whose owner may not diminish the use of the servitude or make it more inconvenient.

defense,equitable compensation,injury avoidance	Damages
Necessity
A person who causes injury under necessity is only liable for equitable damages as determined by the judge, rather than full reparation.

creation,grant,obligation	Mortgage
Mortgagor
The mortgagor grants the mortgage and must be the owner of the mortgaged property with legal capacity to dispose of it, bearing the costs of the authentic document unless otherwise agreed.<SEP>The mortgagor grants the mortgage over their property and is the guarantor of its effectiveness.

duty of diligence,standard of care	Mandatary (الوكيل)
Reasonable Person (الرجل المعتاد)
In a remunerated mandate, the mandatary must always exercise the diligence of a reasonable person in performing the mandate; in a gratuitous mandate, the standard is the care given to own affairs without exceeding the reasonable person threshold.

collective responsibility,multiple principals	Joint and Several Liability (التضامن)
Mandator (الموكل)
When several persons appoint a sole mandatary for a common purpose, they are jointly and severally liable to the mandatary regarding the consequences of performing the mandate.

data.src_id: Book IV: Accessory Rights Or Real Securities
data.content:
code structure,hierarchy	Book IV: Accessory Rights Or Real Securities
Chapter I: Mortgages
Book IV contains Chapter I, which specifically governs mortgages as part of the broader framework of accessory real rights and real securities.

benefit,legal right,use and preservation	Dominant Tenement
Servitude
A servitude is established for the benefit of the dominant tenement, entitling its owner to use and preserve the right in the least harmful manner possible.

equal division,multiple tortfeasors,shared responsibility	Damages
Joint and Several Liability
When several persons are responsible for an injury, they are jointly and severally liable for damages, shared equally unless the judge assigns individual shares.

benefit,creditor right,preference	Mortgage
Mortgagee Creditor
The mortgagee creditor benefits from the mortgage, acquiring a real right of preference over ordinary and subordinate creditors for payment of the claim from the proceeds of the mortgaged property.

indemnification,notification,resignation	Mandatary (الوكيل)
Renunciation of Mandate
The mandatary may renounce the mandate at any time by notification to the mandator, but must indemnify for loss if the renunciation is untimely or unjustified in a remunerated mandate, and cannot renounce a mandate in the interest of a third party without serious reasons.

shared liability,unauthorized delegation	Joint and Several Liability (التضامن)
Substitute (نائب الوكيل)
When a mandatary appoints an unauthorized substitute, both the mandatary and the substitute are jointly and severally responsible for the acts performed.

extended prescription,non-user period	Servitude
Wakf Property
A servitude established for the benefit of a wakf property is subject to an extended thirty-three-year non-user period for extinguishment, compared to the standard fifteen-year period.

guarantee,installment payment,judicial order	Damages
Security
When damages are ordered to be paid by installments or as a periodical payment, the debtor may be required to provide security to ensure payment.

formal requirement,validity	Authentic Document
Mortgage
A mortgage can only be validly constituted by an authentic document, without which the mortgage is not legally effective.

capacity,debt security,identity,legal distinction	Debtor
Mortgagor
The mortgagor may be a person other than the debtor; in such case only the mortgaged property may be proceeded against and the mortgagor cannot demand sale of the debtor's property first.<SEP>The mortgagor may be the debtor himself or a third party who consents to the mortgage of his property in the interests of the debtor.

adjudication,damages,redress	Court
Servitude
The Court may grant damages instead of material redress for breaches of servitude restrictions when it considers there are sufficient reasons for doing so.

compensation method,original position,victim demand	Damages
Restoration
Upon the demand of the victim, the judge may order restoration of the original position as an alternative to monetary damages for reparation of an unlawful act.

enforcement,marketability,sale	Mortgage
Public Auction
A mortgaged property must be capable of being sold by public auction, ensuring the mortgagee creditor can enforce the right through sale proceeds.

data.tgt_id: Section I: The Constitution Of Mortgages
data.content:
code structure,hierarchy	Chapter I: Mortgages
Section I: The Constitution Of Mortgages
Chapter I on Mortgages contains Section I, which specifically governs the constitution and formation of mortgages.

contractual obligation,lease agreement,lease relationship,mutual obligations,obligations,privilege enforcement,reciprocal obligations	Lessee
Lessor
The lessor undertakes to enable the lessee to enjoy the leased property for a certain time in return for a fixed rent under the lease contract.<SEP>The lessor and lessee are bound by the agreement of lease, with the lessor granting enjoyment of the property and the lessee paying rent, maintaining the property, and complying with agreed terms.<SEP>The lessor grants the lease to the lessee and is entitled to rent, restituted property, and compensation for unlawful retention, while the lessee is obligated to maintain and return the property and pay rent.<SEP>The Lessor grants leases to the Lessee, creating reciprocal rights and obligations including rent payment, property maintenance, and compensation upon early termination.<SEP>The Lessor has a privilege over the Lessee's attachable movables and crops on the leased property for rent and other sums due under the lease, enforceable for up to two years, as governed by Article 1143.

interruption,prescription,shared rights	Co-Owners In Common
Servitude
Co-owners in common of a dominant tenement share servitude rights; use of the servitude by one co-owner interrupts prescription in favor of all other co-owners.

enjoyment,maintenance,restitution,use,use right	Leased Property
Lessee
The lessee has the right to enjoy the use of the leased property and must not be disturbed by the lessor in such enjoyment.<SEP>The lessee is entitled to use and enjoy the leased property and must restitute it upon expiration of the lease, preserving it with the care of a reasonable person.<SEP>The lessee uses and must restitute the leased property upon expiration in the condition it was received, subject to permissible wear.

consent,reimbursement	Improvements
Lessor
The lessor is bound to reimburse the lessee for improvements that increase the value of the property unless made without the lessor's knowledge or despite objection.

governance,source of rules	Deed Of Creation
Servitude
Servitudes are governed by the rules laid down in the deed by which they are created, as established in Article 1019.

debt obligation,direct liability,sub-lease arrangement,sub-lease relationship	Lessee
Sub-Lessee
The lessee may sublet the property to a sub-lessee, and the sub-lessee becomes directly answerable to the lessor for amounts owed after summons.<SEP>The Sub-Lessee rents from the principal Lessee, and the amount due by the Sub-Lessee to the Lessee determines the scope of the Lessor's privilege when sub-letting was not prohibited, as stated in Article 1143.

advance rent liability,lease binding,ownership transfer,remedy	Lessor
New Owner
The lessor's ownership of the leased property may be transferred to a new owner, who is bound by the lease only if it has an established date prior to the transfer.<SEP>If the new owner cannot prove that the lessee knew of the transfer of ownership at the time advance rent was paid, the new owner has only a remedy against the lessor for those payments.

customary law,governance	Local Custom
Servitude
Local custom serves as one of the governing sources for servitudes alongside the deed of creation and statutory provisions.

assignment,guarantee	Assignee
Lessee
The lessee may assign the lease to an assignee and remains guarantor for the assignee's obligations unless the lessor formally accepts the assignment.

damage recovery,payment obligation	Compensation
Lessor
The lessor is entitled to receive compensation from the lessee for unlawful retention or damage, and must pay compensation to the lessee for early termination or eviction.

extinguishment,modification	Prescription
Servitude
A servitude right can be extinguished through prescription by non-user, and the manner of its exercise may also be modified by prescription.

compensation,eviction	Lessee
New Owner
The new owner may evict the lessee only after providing proper notice under Article 563 and paying compensation, unless the lease is binding on the new owner.

consent,guarantee	Lessor
Surety
The lessor benefits from the surety's guarantee for the lessee's obligations, but the suretyship does not transfer to a tacitly renewed lease without the surety's consent.

extinguishment,lapse of right	Non-User
Servitude
A servitude is extinguished by non-user for a period of fifteen years generally, or thirty-three years if created for the benefit of wakf property.

construction,value increase	Improvements
Lessee
The lessee may erect buildings, plant trees, or make other improvements on the leased property that increase its value and may claim reimbursement.

legal reference,notice periods	Article 563
Lease Contract
The lease contract is governed by the notice periods prescribed in Article 563 for termination, evacuation, and renewal-related procedures.

implied agreement,indefinite lease	Lessor
Tacit Renewal
The lessor's knowledge of and failure to object to the lessee's continued use results in tacit renewal of the lease for an indefinite duration.

accessory,extension,immovable appurtenance	Mortgage
Servitude
A mortgage extends to the accessories of the mortgaged property, including servitudes, improvements, and other works benefiting the owner.

financial duty,lease consideration,payment obligation	Lessee
Rent
The lessee is obligated to pay rent to the lessor, which may consist of money or any other prestation.<SEP>The lessee is obligated to pay rent at agreed times or at times established by local custom, with payment made at the lessee's domicile unless otherwise agreed.<SEP>The lessee is obligated to pay rent to the lessor for the use of the leased property.

continuity of guarantee,transfer	Real Securities
Tacit Renewal
Real securities supplied under the original lease are transferred to the tacitly renewed lease, subject to real property publication rules.

judicial authority,time for settlement	Court
Lessor
The Court may grant the lessor time for settlement when the lessor chooses to keep improvements and pay the lessee, and may maintain a lease despite sub-letting prohibitions.

contractor priority,preserved right,privilege	Article 1148
Mortgage
Article 1148 grants a privilege for sums due to contractors or architects that is preserved without prejudice when a mortgage extends to accessories of the mortgaged property.

inheritance,termination claim	Heirs of Lessee
Lessee
Upon the death of the lessee, the heirs may claim termination of the lease if the burden has become too heavy, provided the claim is made within six months.

resiliation,security demand	Insolvency
Lessor
The lessor may claim resiliation of the lease due to the lessee's insolvency unless adequate securities are provided within a reasonable time.

judicial authorization,lease maintenance	Court
Purchaser
The court may maintain the lease in force for the purchaser of an industrial or commercial establishment despite a prohibition on sub-letting, provided the purchaser furnishes adequate security and the lessor suffers no real prejudice.

protection of creditor,validity	Good Faith
Mortgage
A mortgage remains valid in favor of a mortgagee creditor who acted in good faith at the time of its conclusion, even if the mortgagor's title is later annulled or abolished.

compliance,termination	Lessee
Notice of Evacuation
The lessee must comply with notice of evacuation given by the lessor or new owner, and the lease is not deemed renewed if notice has been given.

delimitation,legal right	Boundary Marks
Owner
Every owner has the right to compel neighbors to place boundary marks on adjoining properties.

no prejudice requirement,security	Lessor
Purchaser
The purchaser must furnish adequate security and ensure that the lessor suffers no real prejudice for the court to maintain the lease despite a sub-letting prohibition.

assimilation,distribution	Fruits And Revenues
Mortgage
From the date of transcription of the formal summons to pay, the fruits and revenues of the mortgaged property are assimilated to the immovable and distributed in the same manner as the property price.

co-proprietorship,repair obligation	Co-owner
Party Wall
Co-proprietors share repair and reconstruction costs of a party wall in proportion to their respective shares.

business operation,creation	Industrial or Commercial Establishment
Lessee
The lessee may create an industrial or commercial establishment on the leased immovable property, and compelling circumstances may require the lessee to sell such establishment.

boundary delimitation,cost sharing	Neighbor
Owner
The cost of placing boundary marks is shared between the owner and the neighbor.

lien,recovery,recovery rights,retention,retention rights	Lessor
Movables
The lessor holds rights of retention and recovery over movables on the leased property, which cannot be exercised if the movables were removed to meet the lessee's professional requirements or if remaining movables sufficiently cover the rent.<SEP>The lessor has a lien on all attachable movables stocking the leased property as security for amounts due under the lease, with the right to object to their removal and to recover them from any possessor even in good faith, subject to the possessor's rights.

enforcement,trigger event	Formal Summons To Pay
Mortgage
The transcription of the formal summons to pay triggers the assimilation of the mortgaged property's fruits and revenues to the immovable for distribution purposes.

legal restriction,property disposition	Contract
Inalienability Clause
A contract may contain an inalienability clause restricting the disposition of property, valid only if based on a legitimate reason and limited to a reasonable duration.

legal evidence,presumption of condition	Lessee
Proces Verbal
If no proces verbal or inventory was drawn at the time of delivery, the lessee is presumed to have received the leased property in good condition, subject to proof to the contrary.

structural modification,usage rights	Owner
Party Wall
An owner of a party wall may use it for its intended purpose, heighten it for good reason, and must bear the cost of heightening and maintenance of the heightened part.

cost bearing,preservation,property ownership,proportional obligation,shared rights,unilateral action	Co-owner
Joint Ownership
Joint ownership involves two or more co-owners holding undivided shares in the same property, with shares presumed equal unless proven otherwise.<SEP>Every co-owner may take necessary preservation measures for the commonly held property even without the consent of other co-owners.<SEP>All co-owners bear management, preservation, tax, and other costs of common property proportionally to their shares.

direct answerability,privilege enforcement,rent payment,sub-letting	Lessor
Sub-Lessee
The sub-lessee is directly answerable to the lessor for amounts owed to the principal lessee from the time a summons is served, and cannot set up advance payments against the lessor unless made before the summons in accordance with custom or a formal agreement.<SEP>The Lessor's privilege extends over movables and crops belonging to the Sub-Lessee if sub-letting was expressly prohibited; if not prohibited, the privilege is limited to amounts due by the Sub-Lessee to the principal Lessee, as stated in Article 1143.

invalidity,void contract	Future Property
Mortgage
A mortgage on future property or property in expectancy is void and cannot be validly constituted.

legal restriction,testamentary disposition	Inalienability Clause
Will
A will may contain an inalienability clause restricting the disposition of property, valid only if based on a legitimate reason and limited to a reasonable duration.

appointment,property management	Court
Manager
The Court may appoint a manager to manage property held in common when co-owners fail to reach a majority decision.

claim,equitable compensation,legal remedy,remedy,termination right	Lessee
Resiliation of Lease
The lessee may demand resiliation of the lease if the leased property is unfit for use, poses a health danger, or is destroyed.<SEP>The lessee may claim resiliation of the lease when deprived of enjoyment due to third-party claims, government acts, trespass, or defects in the property.<SEP>The lessee may claim resiliation of the lease if not authorized to assign the lease or sublet the property, upon payment of equitable compensation.

co-proprietorship acquisition,heightening	Neighbor
Party Wall
A neighbor who did not contribute to heightening expenses may become a co-proprietor of the heightened part by paying half the cost and half the value of any additional ground area.

access rights,easement	Owner
Right of Way
An owner whose land is cut off from a public road may claim a right of way over neighboring property subject to fair compensation.

management,voting rights	Co-owner
Majority Decision
Decisions on ordinary management taken by a majority of co-owners calculated on the basis of share value are binding on all co-owners.

lease enforceability,voluntary or forced transfer	Lessor
Transfer of Ownership
The lessor's ownership of the leased property may be transferred voluntarily or by force to a third party, and the lease is only binding on the new owner if it has an established date prior to the transfer.

exception,legal cross-reference	Article 816
Article 818
Article 818 provides an exception allowing an owner to compel assignment of part of a wall or land only in the case provided for in Article 816.

legal dependency,validity condition	Article 823
Article 824
Article 824 declares alienations void only when the inalienability clause is valid in accordance with the provisions of Article 823.

construction requirements,legal compliance	Establishments Injurious to Neighbors
Regulations
Factories, wells, steam engines, and all establishments injurious to neighbors must be constructed at distances and subject to conditions laid down by regulations.

administration,management authority	Joint Ownership
Manager
A manager, whether appointed by majority or by the Court, administers the commonly held property and may establish binding management rules.

legal restriction,minimum distance	Direct View
Neighbor
A neighbor is not entitled to have a direct view over a neighbor's property at a distance of less than one meter.

protected interest,validity basis	Inalienability Clause
Third Party
An inalienability clause may be deemed valid if its purpose is to protect a lawful interest of a third party, and the reasonable duration may extend for the life of that third party.

easement condition,payment obligation	Fair Compensation
Right of Way
The exercise of a right of way is subject to payment of fair compensation to the neighbor whose land is crossed.

dispute resolution,judicial authority	Co-owner
Court
The Court may take necessary measures upon application of any co-owner when there is no majority, and dissenting co-owners may challenge decisions before the Court within two months of notification.

personal need,termination right	Lessor
Notice of Evacuation
The lessor may give notice of evacuation to the lessee when the lessor has a personal need for the property, provided such right was agreed upon and notice is given in accordance with Article 563.

creditor rights,legal framework	Joint and Several Creditor
Solidarity
Solidarity establishes the legal framework governing the rights of joint and several creditors, including proportional or equal division of received payments.

legal restriction,minimum distance	Neighbor
Oblique View
A neighbor is not entitled to have an oblique view over a neighbor's property at a distance of less than fifty centimeters.

partition adjustment,property transfer	Acquirer
Co-owner
If a co-owner alienates a specific part of common property that does not fall within the co-owner's share upon partition, the acquirer's right transfers to the part that devolves on the co-owner, or the acquirer may demand cancellation if unaware of the co-owner's lack of ownership of that specific part.

claim assignment,transfer	Assignment of a Right
Joint and Several Creditor
Assignment of a right allows a creditor to transfer his claim to a third party, including all associated warranties, securities, privileges, and accrued interest, without requiring the debtor's consent.

debtor liability,legal framework	Joint and Several Debtor
Solidarity
Solidarity establishes the legal principle under which each joint and several debtor is liable for the entire debt, and payment by one liberates all others.

code organization,legal structure	Chapter IV
Transmission of an Obligation
Chapter IV organizes the legal provisions governing the transmission of obligations, including the assignment of rights.

air and light,exemption	Light Shaft Opening
Neighbor
No distance requirement applies to a light shaft opening intended only for air and light without providing a view over the neighbor's property.

property division,share allocation	Co-owner
Partition
Partition divides commonly held property among co-owners into individual portions, and the rights of an acquirer of a specific part are adjusted according to the portion that devolves upon the disposing co-owner after partition.

legal basis,statutory provision	Article 303
Assignment of a Right
Article 303 is the statutory basis for the assignment of a right, establishing the conditions under which a creditor may transfer his claim to a third party.

recourse,shared liability	Co-debtor
Joint and Several Debtor
A joint and several debtor who pays the full debt has a right of recourse against each co-debtor for their respective share, and shares of insolvent co-debtors are borne pro rata by solvent co-debtors.

legal topic,structural hierarchy,structural organization,subdivision	Chapter IV
Section I
Section I is a subdivision of Chapter IV specifically addressing the legal rules on the assignment of a creditor's right to a third party.<SEP>Section I, titled "General Provisions," falls under Chapter IV on Privileged Rights.

proximity,view exception	Neighbor
Public Road
The prohibition on having an oblique view over a neighbor's property ceases to have effect if the oblique view is simultaneously a direct view over a public road.

pre-partition claim,recovery right	Co-owner
Common Movable Property
A co-owner has the right to recover a common share in movable property or a collection of property before partition, as provided in Article 833.

debt release,obligation modification	Joint and Several Debtor
Novation
Novation between a creditor and one joint and several debtor releases other co-debtors unless the creditor expressly reserves his rights against them.

contribution,insolvency	Article 298
Co-debtor
Article 298 provides that the share of an insolvent co-debtor is borne pro rata by the paying co-debtor and all other solvent co-debtors.

role,transfer of claim	Assignment of a Right
Assignor
The assignor is the party who transfers a right in the assignment, warranting the existence of the right in cases of valuable consideration but not warranting the debtor's solvency unless specifically stipulated.

acquired rights,long-term use	Neighbor
Prescription
A neighbor who has acquired by prescription the right to a direct view at less than one meter over a neighbor's property prevents that neighbor from building within one meter along the building where the view was opened.

debt extinguishment,partial effect	Joint and Several Debtor
Merger
Merger in the person of a creditor and one joint and several debtor does not extinguish the debt as regards other co-debtors except to the extent of the merged share.

legal constraint,transferability limit	Assignment of a Right
Attachment
Attachment limits the assignability of a right; a right can only be assigned to the extent that it is capable of being attached.

creditor as transferor,role identity	Assignor
Joint and Several Creditor
The assignor in an assignment of a right is the original creditor who transfers his claim to a third party.

discharge,partial release	Joint and Several Debtor
Release of Debt
Release of debt granted to one joint and several debtor does not release other co-debtors unless the creditor expressly declares such, and the creditor may claim the remaining balance from other co-debtors.

encumbrance,security	Mortgage
Mortgaged Property
The mortgage encumbers the mortgaged property, with every part of the property securing the whole debt and each part of the debt secured by the whole property.<SEP>The Mortgage is a legal encumbrance on the Mortgaged Property serving as security for a debt.

extinction,partial benefit,time limit	Joint and Several Debtor
Prescription
Prescription extinguishing the debt as to one joint and several debtor benefits other co-debtors only to the extent of that debtor's share, and interruption or suspension as to one debtor cannot be invoked against others.

beneficiary,enforcement,holds	Mortgage
Mortgagee
A mortgagee holds the mortgage and may enforce it by taking expropriation proceedings or assigning rank to another creditor.<SEP>The mortgagee holds the mortgage right and may enforce it through expropriation and sale of the mortgaged property.

full liability,obligation type	Indivisibility
Joint and Several Debtor
Under indivisibility, each debtor in an indivisible obligation is liable for the debt in full, and a debtor who pays has recourse against others for their shares.

entitlement,legal privilege,payment,priority	Mortgagee
Right of Preference
The Right of Preference entitles mortgagees to be paid before unsecured creditors from the proceeds of the mortgaged property.<SEP>The mortgagee exercises the right of preference to be paid before ordinary creditors from the proceeds of the mortgaged property.

debt security,obligation	Debtor
Mortgage
The mortgage secures the debt owed by the debtor and cannot be separated from it in terms of validity and extinction.

mutual debts,set-off limitation	Compensation
Joint and Several Debtor
A joint and several debtor cannot invoke compensation between the creditor and another co-debtor except to the extent of that other co-debtor's share.

legal definition,statutory provision	Article 300
Indivisibility
Article 300 provides the statutory definition of indivisibility, specifying when an obligation cannot be divided by nature or by the parties' intention.

substitution,transfer	Mortgaged Property
Right of Tracing
The right of tracing allows the mortgage to follow into substituted assets such as compensation, insurance, or expropriation payments when the mortgaged property perishes or deteriorates.

ranking,registration,validation	Inscription
Mortgage
A mortgage ranks from the date of its inscription, and the inscription has the effect of automatically collocating costs and interest with the mortgage debt.<SEP>Inscription of the mortgage deed or judgment establishes its legal effectiveness and enforceability against third parties.

debt recovery,right of action	Joint and Several Debtor
Subrogation
A joint and several debtor who pays the full debt may exercise subrogation by bringing the creditor's action against other co-debtors, but recovery is limited to each co-debtor's respective share.

allocation,judicial determination	Judge
Partition
The Judge fixes by order on petition the portion of property to which the mortgage is transferred following partition.

enforceability,priority	Inscription
Third Party
The mortgage becomes effective against third parties only if inscribed before they acquire real rights on the property.

enforcement,procedural governance	Code of Procedure
Mortgage
The Code of Procedure governs the delays and formalities for expropriation and sale of the mortgaged property by the creditor.

benefit and consent,settlement	Joint and Several Debtor
Transaction
A transaction between a creditor and one joint and several debtor benefits other co-debtors if it involves remission of the debt, but is binding on others only if they consent when it creates or increases obligations.

enforceability limitation,priority	Lease
Mortgagee
A lease entered into by the mortgagor has limited enforceability against the mortgagee, requiring an established date prior to the formal summons to pay.

injunction,protection	Judge
Mortgaged Property
The Judge may order the cessation of acts that may result in loss or deterioration of the mortgaged property and adopt necessary protective measures.

data.tgt_id: Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
data.content:
governance,registration procedure	Inscription
Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
The Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights governs the procedures for inscription, renewal, radiation, and annulment of registration of real rights.

grant,shared ownership	Co-owner
Mortgage
A co-owner may grant a mortgage on their undivided share or a divided part of the immovable property held in common.

burden sharing,financial inability	Insolvency
Joint and Several Debtor
When a joint and several debtor becomes insolvent, the insolvent debtor's share is borne pro rata by the co-debtor who effected payment and all other solvent co-debtors.

assimilation,trigger	Formal Summons to Pay
Mortgaged Property
From the date of transcription of the formal summons to pay, the fruits and revenues of the mortgaged property are assimilated to the immovable and distributed like the price of the property.

payment order,priority	Ordinary Creditors
Right of Preference
Mortgagees exercise their right of preference to be paid from the proceeds of the mortgaged property before ordinary creditors.

enforceability,registration	Inscription
Subrogation
Legal or contractual subrogation into a right secured by an inscription is enforceable against third parties only if inscribed in the margin of the original inscription.

reallocation,transfer	Mortgage
Partition
Partition of co-owned property may result in the transfer of the mortgage, with its degree of priority, to a portion of newly attributed property of equivalent value.

limited effect,procedural act	Formal Demand
Joint and Several Debtor
A formal demand directed by the creditor at one joint and several debtor has no effect against other co-debtors, but a formal demand by a co-debtor against the creditor benefits all co-debtors.

insolvent share,pro rata contribution	Co-debtor
Insolvency
The share of an insolvent co-debtor is distributed among solvent co-debtors and the paying co-debtor pro rata to their respective shares.

advance payment,enforceability limitation	Assignment of Rent
Mortgagee
An assignment of rent in advance has limited enforceability against the mortgagee, subject to established date and transcription requirements similar to those governing leases.

disposition,management	Mortgaged Property
Mortgagor
The mortgagor may dispose of and manage the mortgaged property and collect its fruits, but any disposal does not affect the right of the mortgagee.

prohibition,void agreement	Mortgage
Pactum Commissorium
A pactum commissorium, which allows the creditor to acquire the mortgaged property at a fixed price upon non-payment or sell it without legal formalities, is void under mortgage law.

non-binding effect,recognition	Acknowledgement of Debt
Joint and Several Debtor
An acknowledgement of debt by one joint and several debtor does not bind the other co-debtors.

legal status,ownership	Co-Owner
Joint Ownership
A co-owner is a participant in joint ownership, holding an undivided share in property held in common.

creditor burden,released debtor contribution	Insolvency
Release of Debt
When a creditor releases a co-debtor from all liability, the creditor bears the released co-debtor's contribution in the share of insolvent co-debtors.

avoidance,surrender	Abandonment of Mortgaged Property
Mortgagor
A mortgagor who is not the debtor may avoid proceedings by abandoning the mortgaged property according to the procedures laid down for abandonment by a third party holder.

compensation,governance	Mortgaged Property
Rules of Accession
The rules of accession determine the compensation owed by the landowner who retains constructions erected by a third party, which compensation becomes subject to the mortgage under Article 1038.

court appointment,valuation	Expert
Summary Court
The Summary Court may delegate one or more experts to value and divide common property into separate parts.

amount fixation,documentation	Mortgage
Mortgage Deed
The mortgage deed is the formal instrument constituting the mortgage and must specify the amount of the secured debt or its maximum attainable amount.

benefit and prejudice,judicial proceeding	Joint and Several Debtor
Oath
An oath refused or tendered by one joint and several debtor does not prejudice the other co-debtors, but an oath taken by a co-debtor at the creditor's request benefits all co-debtors.

legal right,property division	Co-Owner
Partition
Every co-owner has the right to demand partition of property held in common unless bound by law or agreement.

cost,cost bearing,financial obligation	Inscription
Mortgagor
The mortgagor bears the cost of the inscription, its renewal, and its radiation unless an agreement provides otherwise.<SEP>The mortgagor bears the cost of inscription, its renewal, and its radiation unless otherwise agreed between the parties.

enforcement,forced sale	Expropriation
Mortgaged Property
Expropriation is the legal process by which the mortgagee may compel the forced sale of the mortgaged property upon summons to the debtor to pay, governed by the Code of Procedure.

competence,judicial referral	Court of First Instance
Summary Court
The Summary Court refers disputes outside its competence to the Court of First Instance and fixes a date for appearance.

exception,priority rules	Bankruptcy
Mortgage
Bankruptcy provisions create an exception to the general rule that a mortgage is effective against third parties only if inscribed before they acquire real rights on the property.

court decision,selective effect	Joint and Several Debtor
Judgment
A judgment against one joint and several debtor has no effect against other co-debtors, but a judgment in favor of one co-debtor benefits all others unless based on a ground personal to that co-debtor.

legal process,termination	Joint Ownership
Partition
Partition is the legal process through which joint ownership of property is terminated by dividing it among co-owners.

legal right,share recovery	Co-Owner
Right of Repurchase
A co-owner may exercise the right of repurchase to buy back an undivided share sold by another co-owner to a third person.

legal reference,sale procedure	Article 841
Code of Procedure
Article 841 requires that property which cannot be divided in kind be sold in the manner laid down by the Code of Procedure.

substitution,transfer	Expropriation
Right of Tracing
The right of tracing allows the mortgage to follow into expropriation payments for public utility when the mortgaged property is subject to compulsory acquisition.

duration,legal framework	Article 846
Provisional Partition
Article 846 establishes the rules for provisional partition including its maximum duration of five years and conversion to final partition after fifteen years.

permanent indivision,prohibition of partition	Article 850
Obligatory Joint Ownership
Article 850 prohibits co-owners from demanding partition when the purpose of the common property requires it to remain in obligatory joint ownership.

family arrangement,specialized ownership	Family Joint Ownership
Joint Ownership
Family joint ownership is a specific form of joint ownership created by written agreement among family members sharing a common occupation or interest.

legal framework,mutual indemnity	Article 844
Warranty Against Eviction
Article 844 establishes the warranty among co-partitioners against eviction or interference caused by reasons predating the partition, with proportional liability.

property division,temporary arrangement	Partition
Provisional Partition
Provisional partition is a temporary form of partition that may convert into a final partition after fifteen years of continuous possession.

mandatory status,permanent indivision	Joint Ownership
Obligatory Joint Ownership
Obligatory joint ownership is a form of joint ownership in which partition cannot be demanded because the property's purpose requires it to remain undivided.

creation,creation provisions,family agreement,legal basis	Article 851
Family Joint Ownership
Article 851 sets forth the legal basis for creating family joint ownership through written agreement among family members with a common occupation or interest.<SEP>Article 851 establishes the legal basis for creating Family Joint Ownership from inherited or other property by family members with a common occupation or interest.

governance,legal analogy	Article 848
Contract of Lease
Article 848 provides that provisional partition is governed by the provisions of the law relating to contracts of lease insofar as they are not incompatible with its nature.

judicial authority,provisional partition	Article 849
Summary Judge
Article 849 empowers the Summary Judge to order a provisional partition upon the application of one co-owner when co-owners cannot reach agreement.

enjoyment rights,temporary allotment	Co-Owner
Provisional Partition
Co-owners enter into provisional partition by allotting each other the enjoyment of divided parts equal to their shares.

division,property valuation	Expert
Partition
The expert proceeds with the composition of separate parts and valuation of property as part of the partition process.

agency,authorization	Creditor
Representative
The Representative is authorized to receive payment on behalf of the Creditor, and payment to the Representative is deemed valid as if made to the Creditor personally.

fulfillment,obligation,performance,validity	Debtor
Payment
Payment may be made by the debtor, his representative, or a third party, but is only valid if the payer is the owner of that with which he has paid and has the capacity to dispose of it.<SEP>The Debtor is required to make payment as soon as the obligation is definitely created, using the very thing due, unless otherwise agreed or provided by law.

indemnity,mutual obligation	Co-Owner
Warranty Against Eviction
Co-partitioners are bound to warrant each other against eviction or interference due to causes existing before the partition.

creditor opposition,procedural rights	Partition
Personal Creditor
Personal creditors have the right to oppose a partition and must be joined before an action for partition is introduced, with the partition being without effect against opposing creditors if they are excluded.

court treasury,deposit of proceeds	Caisse du Tribunal
Public Auction
Proceeds from a Public Auction are deposited into the Caisse du Tribunal, the court treasury, by order of the judge.

governed by,procedural law	Code of Procedure
Judicial Deposit
The Judicial Deposit must be made in the manner prescribed by the Code of Procedure.

proof of payment,right to demand	Debtor
Receipt
The Debtor has the right to demand a Receipt for partial payment and annotation on the document of title upon making any payment.

equivalent to payment,substitution	Giving in Payment
Payment
Giving in Payment takes the place of Payment when the Creditor accepts another prestation in settlement of the right due.

dissent,legal remedy	Co-Owner
Right of Action
A dissenting co-owner has a right of action before the Court within two months of notification of an alienation decision.

injury threshold,rescission	Article 845
Partition
Article 845 permits rescission of a partition by agreement if a co-partitioner proves injury exceeding one fifth of his share, provided the action is brought within one year.

new obligation,replacement	Novation
Obligation
Novation replaces the original Obligation with a new one, requiring both obligations to be free from grounds of nullity.

cancellation,restitution	Debtor
Document of Title of Debt
The Debtor has the right to demand restitution or cancellation of the Document of Title of Debt upon full payment, or a written declaration of its loss.

alienation,majority decision	Article 832
Co-Owner
Article 832 governs the right of co-owners holding at least three-quarters of common property to decide on alienation.

cessation,financial charge	Interest
Summons
Upon service of a Summons on the Creditor, Interest on the debt ceases to run.

authorization,judicial order	Court
Judicial Deposit
The Court authorizes the Judicial Deposit upon application by the Debtor when the Creditor refuses payment or other justified circumstances exist.

debt discharge,extinction	Giving in Payment
Obligation
Giving in Payment extinguishes the Obligation when the Creditor accepts a substitute prestation, with provisions of sale and payment applying accordingly.

change of creditor,obligation change,party substitution,substitution	Creditor
Novation
Novation may be effected by a change of the Creditor when the Creditor, Debtor, and a third party agree that the third party shall be the new Creditor.<SEP>Novation may be effected by a change of the creditor, requiring agreement among the creditor, debtor, and third party.

creditor rights,opposition	Article 842
Co-Owner
Article 842 grants personal creditors of any co-owner the right to oppose partition proceedings without their intervention.

discharge,safekeeping	Debtor
Judicial Deposit
The Debtor may resort to Judicial Deposit when the Creditor refuses payment, is unknown, incapable, or when the debt is disputed between several persons.

court order,safekeeping	Court
Judicial Custody
The Court may order Judicial Custody of immovable property or things intended to remain in place at the Debtor's request.

consent,participation,party substitution,substitution	Novation
Third Party
