A third party may become the new debtor or new creditor through novation with the consent of the original parties.<SEP>The Third Party participates in Novation by agreeing to substitute the original Debtor or by becoming the new Creditor through tripartite agreement.

formal notice,legal process	Creditor
Summons
The Summons is served on the Creditor, after which the Creditor becomes responsible for loss or deterioration of the thing due.

dispute resolution,legal proceedings	Co-Owner
Summary Court
A co-owner who wishes to withdraw from joint ownership may summon other co-owners before the Summary Court when agreement on partition cannot be reached.

equivalence to payment,sequence	Actual Tender
Judicial Deposit
Actual Tender must be followed by a Judicial Deposit or equivalent measure for it to be considered equivalent to payment.

court-authorized sale,perishable goods	Debtor
Public Auction
The Debtor may sell perishable or costly-to-store items by Public Auction with the permission of the judge and deposit the proceeds in the Caisse du Tribunal.

imputation order,payment allocation	Expenses
Principal
When an insufficient payment is made, Expenses are deducted first, then interest, and lastly the Principal of the debt.

confirmation,ratification,validity	Novation
Voidable Contract
Novation is only valid in the context of a voidable contract if the new obligation is intended to confirm the contract and replace the original obligation.<SEP>Novation of an obligation arising from a Voidable Contract is only valid if the new obligation is intended to ratify and replace the original voidable contract.

agreement,consent,debt assumption,payment,subrogation,subrogation agreement	Creditor
Third Party
A third party who pays off a debt is subrogated into the rights of the creditor who has been paid off, acquiring all attributes, securities, and defenses of the debt.<SEP>The Third Party agrees with the Creditor to take the place of the original Debtor, releasing the original Debtor without the original Debtor's consent being necessary.<SEP>A creditor who receives payment from a third party may by agreement with the third party subrogate such third party into his rights even without the debtor's consent, provided the agreement is made at the time of payment.

creditor rights,opposition	Co-Owner
Personal Creditor
Personal creditors of a co-owner may oppose partition in kind or sale by auction without their intervention, and such opposition compels all co-owners to join them in every stage of the proceedings.

payment order,priority	Mortgagee
Unsecured Creditor
Mortgagees are paid before unsecured creditors out of the proceeds of sale of the mortgaged property, in accordance with the Right of Preference.

court recognition,validation	Actual Tender
Final Judgment
Actual Tender is recognized as valid if confirmed by a Final Judgment, at which point the Debtor's retraction releases co-debtors and sureties.

acquisition,purge rights	Mortgage
Third Party Holder
A third party holder acquires the mortgaged property without personal liability for the debt and may purge the property of all mortgages under prescribed procedures.

change of debtor,obligation change,party substitution,release	Debtor
Novation
Novation may be effected by a change of the Debtor when a third party agrees to take the place of the original Debtor, releasing the original Debtor from the obligation.<SEP>Novation may be effected by a change of the debtor, substituting a third party as the new debtor with the creditor's consent.

deemed ownership,retroactive title	Article 843
Co-Owner
Article 843 deems each co-partitioner to have been the owner of the part falling to him from the date he became co-owner in common.

data.src_id: Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
data.content:
governance,legal framework	Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
Mortgage
The inscription, renewal, radiation, and annulment of radiation of mortgages are governed by the Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights.

property acquisition,reimbursement	Former Owner
Third Party Holder
The third party holder has a claim for reimbursement against the former owner of the mortgaged property for all amounts paid to satisfy creditors.

priority,temporal order	Inscription
Rank Assignment
The rank of a mortgage is determined from the date of its inscription, establishing the order of payment among mortgagees.

joint liability,shared obligation	Co-debtor
Debtor
The Co-debtor shares responsibility for the debt with the Debtor and is not freed if the Debtor retracts a tender before acceptance or valid judgment.

clearance,legal procedure,legal process,property clearance	Purge
Third Party Holder
The third party holder may initiate the purge process to clear the property of all inscriptions by serving formal summons on inscribed creditors and offering to pay inscribed debts up to the valued amount.<SEP>The Third Party Holder may choose to purge the mortgaged property of all inscriptions by paying the sum at which the property is valued to creditors or depositing it at the Caisse of the Court.

formalities,procedural requirement	Compulsory Expropriation
Public Auction
When an application is made for the sale of the property, the formalities laid down for compulsory expropriation must be followed in conducting the public auction.

consent,opposition,payment,refusal of payment,remedy,substitution	Debtor
Third Party
A third party who pays off the debt has a remedy against the debtor up to the amount paid, though the debtor may contest the claim if he had any interest in opposing the payment.<SEP>The Debtor may procure the Creditor's consent to substitute the Debtor with a Third Party who consents to be the new Debtor.<SEP>A creditor may refuse payment tendered by a third party if the debtor opposes it and has informed the creditor of his opposition.

cost liability,refund	Purchaser by Auction
Third Party Holder
The purchaser by auction is liable to refund the disposed third party holder for costs of the deed, its transcription, and summons served.

opposition,sale application	Inscribed Creditor
Purge
Every inscribed creditor has the right to apply for the sale of the property being purged within thirty days of the last formal summons, potentially leading to a public auction.

legal procedure,recording	Greffier of the Court
Insolvency
The Greffier of the Court records the judgment ending the state of insolvency in the margin of the registration on the day the judgment is delivered.

burden of payment,cost allocation	Debtor
Expenses
The Debtor bears the Expenses in connection with payment unless an agreement or legal provision provides otherwise.

affiliation,judicial administration	Cairo Court
Registrar of the Cairo Court
The Registrar of the Cairo Court serves within the Cairo Court and makes registration entries on its behalf.

debt payment,enforcement,expropriation,legal obligations	Mortgagee
Third Party Holder
A mortgagee may, upon maturity of the debt, take expropriation proceedings against the third party holder unless the third party holder chooses to pay the debt, redeem the mortgage, or abandon the property.<SEP>The Third Party Holder must pay inscribed debts or face expropriation proceedings initiated by the Mortgagee, and the Mortgagee must summon the Third Party Holder before initiating expropriation.

enforcement,legal recourse	Creditor
Judge
The creditor may apply to the judge to fix terms for the debtor's election, demand additional security, and take proceedings to enforce obligations.

opposition,sale application	Purge
Surety
Every surety of an inscribed debt has the right to apply for the sale of the property that a third party holder wishes to purge.

condition type,legal classification	Conditional Obligation
Suspensive Condition
A suspensive condition is a form of conditional obligation where the obligation does not become executory until the condition is realized, as defined in Articles 267 and 268.

delay,grace period	Court
Debtor
The Court may grant the Debtor one or more reasonable delays for performance of the obligation in exceptional cases where no serious prejudice is caused to the Creditor.

communication,legal procedure	Greffier of the Court
Registrar of the Cairo Court
The Greffier sends a copy of the judgment ending insolvency to the Registrar of the Cairo Court for the purpose of making a similar registration entry.

payment obligation,procedural notice	Inscribed Creditor
Third Party Holder
The third party holder must serve formal summons on inscribed creditors when purging the property and may be compelled by inscribed creditors to pay debts if the amount owed is sufficient.

benefit,procedural effect	Formal Summons to Pay
Mortgagee
The transcription of a formal summons to pay by one creditor benefits all other creditors of the mortgaged property.

condition types,legal contrast	Resolutory Condition
Suspensive Condition
A suspensive condition determines the existence of an obligation, while a resolutory condition determines its extinction; both are governed by rules on void conditions in Article 266.

debt discharge,substitution of performance	Debtor
Giving in Payment
The Debtor may satisfy the obligation through Giving in Payment by providing the Creditor with a different prestation than what was originally due, provided the Creditor accepts it.

deposit,judicial oversight	Court
Purge
The Court receives deposits from the third party holder or applicant to cover costs and satisfies creditors, and the conditions of sale are filed before the Court.

obligation extinguishment,restitution	Creditor
Resolutory Condition
Upon realization of the resolutory condition, the creditor must restitute what has been received and is liable in damages if restitution is impossible due to a cause for which the creditor is responsible.

retroactivity,term expiration	Retroactive Effect
Time Clause
The extinction of an obligation at the end of a resolutory term has no retroactive effect, as stated in Article 274, distinguishing it from the retroactive effect of resolutory conditions.

offer,performance	Actual Tender
Debtor
The Debtor makes the Actual Tender of the thing due and may retract it as long as it has not been accepted by the Creditor or recognized as valid by a Final Judgment.

deposit,financial obligation	Applicant
Court
The applicant must deposit at the Caisse of the Court a sum sufficient to cover the cost of the sale by auction and has no right to a refund if the auction does not yield a higher price than the third party holder's offer.

condition type,legal classification	Conditional Obligation
Resolutory Condition
A resolutory condition is a form of conditional obligation where the obligation is extinguished upon realization of the condition, as defined in Article 269.

debt collection,joint rights	Creditor
Solidarity
Under solidarity, joint and several creditors may take proceedings jointly or severally against the debtor, and amounts received are divided proportionally among all creditors.

excess payment,payment,subrogation	Debtor
Third Party Holder
A third party holder may pay the secured debt and its accessories upon maturity and is subrogated into the rights of the satisfied creditor, with a claim for reimbursement against the debtor.<SEP>The Third Party Holder has a right of action against the Debtor for sums paid in excess of what is due under the title deed and is subrogated into the rights of creditors discharged.

contractual parties,debt assignment,mortgage,obligations,property transfer,reciprocal obligations,sale,sale contract,sale transaction,transfer of ownership	Purchaser
Vendor
The Vendor transfers ownership of the thing sold to the Purchaser, and must allow the Purchaser sufficient acquaintance and trial of the thing where applicable.<SEP>The vendor and purchaser may agree to assign the mortgage debt in connection with the sale of mortgaged immovable property, requiring creditor ratification or refusal within six months of notification.<SEP>The vendor and purchaser are the two primary parties to a sale contract, with the vendor obligated to deliver the thing sold and the purchaser obligated to pay the price and bear costs of the deed.<SEP>The vendor is bound to the purchaser to transfer ownership, deliver the thing sold, and provide warranty against disturbance and eviction.<SEP>The Vendor and the Purchaser are the two contracting parties in the sale contract, with the Vendor obligated to deliver the thing sold and provide warranties, and the Purchaser obligated to pay the price and inspect the thing sold.<SEP>The Vendor sells property to the Purchaser, and both must be notified of any intention to exercise preemption within fifteen days of a formal summons.

condition fulfillment,retroactivity	Conditional Obligation
Retroactive Effect
The fulfillment of a condition in a conditional obligation is effective retroactively to the day the obligation was contracted, unless the will of the parties or the nature of the contract indicates otherwise, as stated in Article 270.

protective measures,security demand	Creditor
Time Clause
Before the expiration of a suspensive term, the creditor may take measures to protect his rights and demand security if he reasonably fears the debtor's bankruptcy or insolvency.

forced redemption,forfeiture,insolvency,legal consequence	Bankruptcy
Debtor
Declaration of bankruptcy or insolvency causes the debtor to forfeit the benefit of the term on obligations, as stated in Article 273.<SEP>The debtor's bankruptcy or insolvency constitutes grounds for compelling the debtor to redeem the annuity.

compliance,legal duty	Obligations Of The Vendor
Vendor
The vendor is subject to the obligations of transfer, delivery, and warranty as prescribed by law.

conditional acceptance,trial period	Purchaser
Sale Upon Trial
The purchaser has the right to accept or reject the thing sold during a trial period, with silence after the agreed time constituting acceptance.

collateral demand,creditor protection	Creditor
Security
The creditor may demand additional security if the debtor diminishes the original security, and may ask for security before the expiration of a suspensive term if there is reasonable fear of the debtor's bankruptcy or insolvency, as stated in Articles 273 and 274.

obligation performance,option right	Alternative Obligation
Debtor
The debtor has the right of election in alternative obligations and is freed entirely upon performance of one of the multiple prestations, as stated in Article 275.

lesion protection,price supplement	Legally Incapable Person
Vendor
The vendor may be required to supplement the price when selling an immovable belonging to a legally incapable person with lesion exceeding one fifth.

legal remedy,price adjustment	Lesion
Supplement Of Price Action
The supplement of price action is a remedy available when lesion exceeds one fifth of the value of an immovable sold by a legally incapable person.

conditional acceptance,tasting	Purchaser
Sale Subject To Tasting
The purchaser may accept the thing sold based on tasting and must declare acceptance within the time fixed by agreement or custom.

legal action,safeguarding rights	Creditor
Protective Measures
The creditor may take protective measures to safeguard his rights before the realization of a suspensive condition or before the expiration of a suspensive term, as provided in Articles 268 and 274.

obligation performance,substitution right	Debtor
Facultative Obligation
In a facultative obligation, the debtor may free himself by performing a substitute prestation in place of the principal prestation promised.

obligation,property conveyance	Ownership Transfer
Vendor
The vendor is responsible for effecting the transfer of ownership of the thing sold to the purchaser.

deferred payment,ownership condition	Credit Sale
Installment Payment
In a credit sale with installment payments, the vendor may stipulate that ownership transfer is subject to integral payment of all installments.

exemption,legal procedure	Lesion
Public Auction
An action for supplement of price on grounds of lesion does not lie in respect of sales by public auction conducted in accordance with the law.

market reference,price agreement	Price Determination
Purchaser
The purchaser is affected by the method of price determination, which may rely on the market price when no specific price is fixed.

condition realization,obligation to return	Creditor
Restitution
Upon realization of a resolutory condition, the creditor must restitute what has been received and is liable in damages if restitution is impossible due to a cause for which the creditor is responsible, as stated in Article 269.

debt performance,joint liability	Debtor
Solidarity
Under solidarity between debtors, payment by one debtor liberates all other debtors from the obligation, as stated in Article 284.

contractual obligation,transfer of possession	Delivery
Vendor
The vendor is bound to deliver the thing sold to the purchaser in its proper state, including accessories and permanent appurtenances.

disadvantage,legal protection	Legally Incapable Person
Lesion
A legally incapable person is protected against lesion exceeding one fifth of the value of their immovable property.

disturbance source,legal claim	Third Party
Warranty Against Disturbance
A third party holding a right over the thing sold may cause disturbance to the purchaser, triggering the vendor's warranty obligation.

price adjustment,quantity dispute	Deficiency And Excess
Purchaser
The purchaser has the right to demand price reduction or contract cancellation when there is a deficiency in the quantity of the thing sold.

creditor actions,validity preservation	Acts of Management
Creditor
Acts of management carried out by the creditor retain their validity notwithstanding the realization of the resolutory condition, as stated in Article 269.

obligation timing,term benefit	Debtor
Time Clause
The debtor benefits from the term of an obligation, but forfeits this benefit if declared bankrupt or insolvent, diminishes security given to the creditor, or fails to supply promised security, as stated in Article 273.

damages reduction,judicial discretion	Installment Payment
Judge
The judge has the authority to reduce agreed damages in installment payment contracts according to circumstances, as referenced in Article 224.

conditional sale,legal structure	Sale Upon Trial
Suspensive Condition
A sale upon trial is deemed to have been made subject to a suspensive condition of acceptance of the thing sold, unless the agreement or circumstances indicate a resolutory condition applies.

legal guarantee,protection	Vendor
Warranty Against Disturbance
The vendor guarantees the purchaser against disturbance in enjoyment of the thing sold, whether caused by the vendor or a third party.

contract dissolution,refund	Perishment Before Delivery
Purchaser
If the thing sold perishes before delivery due to a cause beyond the vendor's control, the purchaser is entitled to dissolution of the sale and a refund of the price.

legal characterization,substance over form	Contract Of Lease
Credit Sale
The provisions governing credit sales, including ownership transfer conditions and installment payment rules, apply even if the contracting parties describe their contract as a contract of lease.

good faith protection,real rights	Supplement Of Price Action
Third Party
The supplement of price action does not operate to the prejudice of third parties in good faith who have acquired a real right on the immovable sold.

exception,retroactivity	Debtor
Retroactive Effect
A condition will not have retroactive effect if the execution of the obligation becomes impossible before fulfillment of the condition on account of a cause independent of the debtor and for which the debtor is not responsible, as stated in Article 270.

property type,valuation	Immovable Property
Lesion
Lesion is assessed by determining the value of the immovable property at the time of sale to ascertain whether the loss exceeds one fifth of its value.

damages reduction,legal cross-reference	Article 224
Article 430
Article 430 paragraph 2 references Article 224 as the legal basis for the judge to reduce agreed damages in installment payment contracts.

alternative condition,conditional sale	Resolutory Condition
Sale Upon Trial
A sale upon trial may alternatively be made subject to a resolutory condition instead of a suspensive condition, as determined by the agreement or circumstances.

price agreement,trade price	Contracting Parties
Price Determination
The contracting parties may fix the price for the thing sold or, if no price is fixed, the sale is not void if they intended to adopt the current trade price or their usual dealing price.

defense obligation,legal intervention	Revendication Action
Vendor
The vendor must join as co-defendant or take the purchaser's place in a revendication action upon receiving proper notice.

property acquisition,rights	Ownership Transfer
Purchaser
The purchaser acquires ownership of the thing sold, which may be subject to conditions such as full payment in a credit sale.

legal arrangement,ownership	Co-owners
Family Joint Ownership
Family Joint Ownership is created and held by co-owners who are members of the same family with a common occupation or interest.

collateral obligation,forfeiture	Debtor
Security
The debtor must not diminish the special security given to the creditor by his own act, and failure to provide promised security causes the debtor to forfeit the benefit of the term, as stated in Article 273.

property law,shared ownership	Common Parts
Ownership of Storeys in Buildings
Ownership of Storeys in Buildings designates Common Parts as indivisible portions co-owned proportionally by all building owners.

contractual agreement,payment terms	Contracting Parties
Installment Payment
The contracting parties may agree on installment payments, including terms for the vendor retaining part of the price as damages upon cancellation.

price supplement,quantity liability	Deficiency And Excess
Vendor
The vendor is liable for deficiencies and entitled to a supplement of the price for excess quantities in the thing sold.

legal process,procedural law	Code Of Procedure
Revendication Action
The Code of Procedure governs the vendor's obligation to intervene in a revendication action brought against the purchaser.

appointment,execution of decisions	Representative of the Syndicate
Syndicate of Owners
The Syndicate of Owners appoints a Representative of the Syndicate to carry out its decisions and manage common parts.

cancellation option,price reduction	Deterioration Before Delivery
Purchaser
The purchaser has the option to cancel the sale or uphold it at a reduced price if the thing sold deteriorates before delivery.

dispute resolution,judicial oversight	Court
Family Joint Ownership
The Court has authority to authorize early withdrawal of shares from Family Joint Ownership and to discharge its manager.

appointment,discharge	Co-owners
Manager
Co-owners who own the majority in value of shares appoint and may discharge the Manager.

repair obligations,structural dependency	Lower Storey
Upper Storey
The owner of the Lower Storey is obligated to execute repairs to prevent the Upper Storey from falling, and the owner of the Upper Storey may not heighten the building so as to injure the Lower Storey.

co-ownership,shared infrastructure	Building
Common Parts
A Building contains Common Parts including foundations, main walls, entrances, yards, roofs, lifts, passages, and pipes intended for common use by all owners.

knowledge,warranty obligation	Good Faith
Vendor
The vendor's liability under the warranty of eviction may be affected by whether the vendor acted in good or bad faith, particularly regarding compensation for the purchaser's expenses.

data.src_id: President of the Court of First Instance
data.content:
judicial appointment,oversight	President of the Court of First Instance
Representative of the Syndicate
The President of the Court of First Instance may appoint or discharge the Representative of the Syndicate when the required majority of owners is not obtained.

compensation,legal protection	Purchaser
Warranty Of Eviction
The purchaser is entitled to compensation under the warranty of eviction, including refund of amounts paid to avoid dispossession along with legal interest and expenses.

co-ownership rules,legal definition	Article 856
Ownership of Storeys in Buildings
Article 856 defines the legal framework for Ownership of Storeys in Buildings, establishing that different owners are co-owners of the ground and common parts.

decision-making authority,governance	Article 864
Syndicate of Owners
Article 864 grants the Syndicate of Owners the right to manage common parts through binding majority decisions when no management rules exist.

appointment,management	Family Joint Ownership
Manager
A Manager is appointed by co-owners holding the majority in value of shares to administer Family Joint Ownership.

judicial enforcement,sale order	Court
Lower Storey
The Court may order the sale of the Lower Storey if its owner refuses to execute necessary repairs to prevent the Upper Storey from falling.

contractual override,legal provisions	Common Parts
Title Deeds
Title Deeds may contain provisions that override the default legal rules regarding co-ownership and designation of Common Parts in a building.

appointment,duties	Article 866
Representative of the Syndicate
Article 866 governs the appointment, duties, and court representation authority of the Representative of the Syndicate.

collective management,governance	Building
Syndicate of Owners
A Building divided into storeys or apartments may be collectively managed by a Syndicate of Owners formed by the individual owners.

priority claims,rights preservation	Compensation
Registered Creditors
Registered Creditors retain their rights when Compensation for building destruction is allocated for reconstruction costs, ensuring their registered claims are not prejudiced.

legal foundation,partition restriction	Article 850
Family Joint Ownership
Article 850 establishes the principle that co-owners cannot demand partition when the property is intended to always remain in common, which underpins Family Joint Ownership.

judicial enforcement,repair orders	Judge
Lower Storey
The Judge may order the sale of the Lower Storey or the execution of urgent repairs if its owner refuses to carry out necessary structural works.

cost sharing,maintenance obligations	Co-owners
Common Parts
Co-owners must participate in the costs of preservation, maintenance, management, and reconstruction of Common Parts in proportion to the value of their shares.

share disposal restriction,unanimous consent	Article 853
Non-family Member
Article 853 restricts disposal of co-owner shares to a Non-family Member without the unanimous consent of all co-owners.

governing law,legal reference	Article 855
Joint Property
Article 855 references Joint Property rules as supplementary law governing Family Joint Ownership.

insurance authorization,risk management	Collective Insurance
Syndicate of Owners
The Syndicate of Owners may take out Collective Insurance against risks to the building or to co-owners jointly, with the prescribed majority consent per Article 865.

party property,shared ownership	Building
Inner Walls
Inner Walls separating two apartments in a Building are owned as party property by the owners of those two apartments.

duration,withdrawal rights	Article 852
Family Joint Ownership
Article 852 limits the duration of Family Joint Ownership to fifteen years and provides mechanisms for early withdrawal.

enforcement,judicial authority	Article 859
Judge
Article 859 grants the Judge authority to order the sale of a lower storey or urgent repairs when the lower storey owner refuses necessary maintenance.

cost recovery,rebuilding rights	Article 860
Upper Storey
Article 860 grants the owner of the Upper Storey the right to rebuild the lower storey at the lower owner's cost and to withhold occupancy until repayment.

cost obligation,maintenance	Article 858
Common Parts
Article 858 obliges every owner to participate in the costs of preservation, maintenance, management, and reconstruction of Common Parts in proportion to the value of their share.

priority protection,rights preservation	Article 868
Registered Creditors
Article 868 preserves the rights of Registered Creditors when compensation for building destruction is allocated for reconstruction.

governing law,legal reference	Article 855
Mandate
Article 855 references Mandate rules as supplementary law governing Family Joint Ownership.

collective decision-making,membership	Co-owners
Syndicate of Owners
Co-owners in a building may form a Syndicate of Owners and are bound by its decisions taken by majority based on share value.

authorization,risk management	Article 865
Collective Insurance
Article 865 authorizes the syndicate to take out Collective Insurance against risks to the building or co-owners.

ownership,rights and obligations	Mortgaged Property
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder holds the mortgaged property with specific rights including purge, abandonment, auction participation, and obligations including restitution of fruits and liability for deterioration.

destruction recovery,reconstruction funding	Building
Compensation
Compensation arising from the destruction of a Building shall be set aside for the costs of reconstruction as decided by the Syndicate of Owners.

governed by,legal framework	Family Joint Ownership
Joint Property
Family Joint Ownership is governed by the rules of Joint Property as stated in Article 855.

data.tgt_id: Section III: Extinguishment of the Mortgage
data.content:
legal termination,statutory provision	Mortgage
Section III: Extinguishment of the Mortgage
Section III governs the extinguishment of the Mortgage, which occurs when the secured debt is extinguished, purge formalities are completed, or compulsory sale proceeds are deposited.

consent requirement,share acquisition	Co-owners
Non-family Member
Co-owners must unanimously consent for a Non-family Member to acquire or be assigned a share of a co-owner in Family Joint Ownership.

enforcement,legal action	Expropriation
Mortgagee
The Mortgagee may initiate expropriation proceedings against the Third Party Holder in accordance with the Code of Procedure after summoning the holder to pay or abandon the property.

deterioration,payment obligation,personal liability,subrogation	Creditor
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder must pay creditors whose rank entitles them to payment, and is subrogated into the rights of creditors discharged by payment.<SEP>The Third Party Holder is personally liable towards creditors for any deterioration caused to the mortgaged property by negligence.

authorization,judicial order	Judgment Charge
President of the Court
The President of the Court reviews applications, considers the debt amount and property value, and issues orders authorizing Judgment Charges, potentially restricting the charge to specific properties.

allocation,reconstruction funding	Article 868
Compensation
Article 868 provides that Compensation due on account of building destruction shall be set aside for reconstruction costs without prejudice to registered creditors' rights.

governed by,legal framework	Family Joint Ownership
Mandate
Family Joint Ownership is governed by the rules of Mandate as stated in Article 855.

declaration,legal procedure	Abandonment
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder may abandon the mortgaged property by submitting a declaration to the Registrar of the Court of First Instance and notifying the creditor conducting expropriation within five days.

administrative duty,notification	Greffier
Judgment Charge
The Greffier is responsible for notifying the debtor of the Judgment Charge order, endorsing it on the judgment copy, and informing the court that rendered the original judgment on the same day.

legal framework,procedural law	Code of Procedure
Expropriation
The Code of Procedure governs the expropriation proceedings that may be taken against the owner, third party holder, or receiver.

consent requirement,restricted entry	Family Joint Ownership
Non-family Member
A Non-family Member may only become a partner in Family Joint Ownership if he and all co-owners consent thereto, per Article 853.

bidding condition,participation	Auction
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder may participate in the auction on condition of not offering a price lower than the sum still owed on the property.

declaration filing,jurisdiction	Abandonment
Court of First Instance
Declarations of abandonment of mortgaged property are submitted to the Registrar of the competent Court of First Instance.

application,legal right,security interest,security right	Creditor
Judgment Charge
A Creditor who has obtained an enforceable judgment may apply for a Judgment Charge on the Debtor's immovable property as security for principal, interest, and costs.<SEP>The creditor may apply for a judgment charge to secure the debt owed by the debtor and has the same rights as a mortgagee once the charge is granted.

compulsory expropriation,forced sale	Auction
Mortgaged Property
The Mortgaged Property may be sold by public auction as part of expropriation proceedings, extinguishing mortgage rights upon deposit or payment of the purchase price.

legal recourse,warranty claim	Preceding Owner
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder has a right of action for warranty against the Preceding Owner to the extent a successor in title has against the person from whom property was acquired.

data.src_id: Chapter II: Judgment Charges upon Immovable Property
data.content:
governed by,statutory framework	Chapter II: Judgment Charges upon Immovable Property
Judgment Charge
Chapter II governs the constitution and procedures for obtaining a Judgment Charge on immovable property, including eligibility requirements and application procedures.

legal basis,prerequisite	Creditor
Enforceable Judgment
A Creditor must obtain an Enforceable Judgment rendered on the merits condemning the Debtor to a liquidated amount before obtaining a Judgment Charge.

compulsory sale,legal process	Auction
Expropriation
The Auction is the mechanism through which expropriation is effected, resulting in the transfer of ownership and extinguishment of mortgage rights.

appointment,property management	Receiver
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder may be appointed as receiver if applying to the Judge Des Referes during expropriation proceedings.

appeal,legal challenge,legal obligation,property encumbrance	Debtor
Judgment Charge
The debtor may lodge an appeal against the order authorizing a judgment charge, either before the judge who issued it or before the Court of First Instance.<SEP>The Debtor's specific immovable properties may be encumbered by a Judgment Charge as security for the debt owed to the Creditor, but no Judgment Charge may be taken after the Debtor's death on property in the estate.

enforceability,legal limitation	Creditor
Foreign Court
A Creditor cannot obtain a Judgment Charge based on a judgment rendered by a Foreign Court until that judgment has been made enforceable.

re-vested rights,real rights	Servitudes
Third Party Holder
Servitudes and other real rights previously held by the Third Party Holder on the property before acquisition are re-vested in the Third Party Holder.

appointment,property management	Judge Des Referes
Receiver
The Judge Des Referes has the authority to appoint a Receiver against whom expropriation proceedings may be taken when a party with interest requests expedition of the sale.

grantor,legal obligation	Donor
Gift
The donor is the party who makes the gift and is bound by obligations regarding delivery, warranty, and revocation.

legal prerequisite,statutory requirement	Enforceable Judgment
Judgment Charge
An Enforceable Judgment is a required legal basis for obtaining a Judgment Charge on immovable property, and certain types of judgments such as those confirming a compromise or agreement are acceptable, while judgments as to validity of a signature are not.

enforceability,legal limitation	Arbitration Award
Creditor
A Creditor cannot obtain a Judgment Charge based on an Arbitration Award until the award has been made enforceable.

fund deposit,payment mechanism	Caisse of the Court
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder may deposit sums for property valuation, auction prices, or debt payments at the Caisse of the Court as an alternative to direct payment to creditors.

legal rights,recipient	Donee
Gift
The donee is the party who receives the gift and acquires rights to delivery, warranty protection, and obligations regarding consideration.

legal grounds,revocation rights	Donor
Revocation of Gift
The donor may initiate revocation of the gift either with the donee's consent or by court application based on reasonable grounds.

data.tgt_id: Section I: The Constitution of a Judgment Charge
data.content:
legal governance,statutory framework	Judgment Charge
Section I: The Constitution of a Judgment Charge
Section I governs the creation, eligibility requirements, and procedural steps for establishing a Judgment Charge on immovable property, including the application process and judicial authorization.

ownership proof,transcription	Third Party Holder
Title Deed
The Third Party Holder transcribes the Title Deed to establish ownership and is deemed owner by virtue of the original Title Deed upon acquiring the property at auction.

compensation,conditional gift	Gift
Valuable Consideration
Valuable consideration may be attached to a gift, affecting the donor's warranty obligations and the donee's performance requirements.

delivery obligation,legal duty	Article 493
Donor
Article 493 obligates the donor to deliver the gifted thing to the donee when the donee has not taken possession.

consent,revocation procedure	Article 500
Revocation of Gift
Article 500 establishes the conditions under which a gift may be revoked, requiring either donee consent or court authorization.

liability,restitution obligation	Fruits of the Property
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder must restitute Fruits of the Property from the date of being summoned to pay or abandon, or from a new summons if proceedings are abandoned for three years.

governing provision,legal rule	Article 491
Gift
Article 491 governs gifts of specific things not belonging to the donor by reference to Articles 466 and 467.

delivery obligation,gift contract,obligations,warranty	Donee
Donor
The donor transfers property to the donee without consideration, and may impose specific obligations on the donee; the donee must accept the gift for it to be complete.<SEP>The donor is obligated to deliver the gifted thing to the donee and has limited warranty obligations for dispossession and defects.

ingratitude,reasonable grounds	Article 501
Revocation of Gift
Article 501 enumerates specific reasonable grounds for revocation including ingratitude, financial inability, and birth of a child.

creditor rights,legal substitution	Subrogation
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder is subrogated into the rights of creditors discharged by payment, including guarantees furnished by the Debtor but excluding those furnished by other parties.

contractual participation,contribution,debt liability,liability,membership,obligations,personal liability,rights	Partner
Partnership
Partners are personally liable for Partnership debts not covered by Partnership assets, each in proportion to his share in the losses, and any agreement relieving a Partner from such liability is void.<SEP>A Partner is a member of the Partnership who contributes capital, services, or other assets and is entitled to a share of profits while being liable for losses and partnership debts.<SEP>Partners contribute property, services, or other assets to a partnership and share in its profits or losses.<SEP>Partners are members of the partnership with mutual obligations, the right to request dissolution, and entitlement to share in assets or losses upon liquidation.

future property,voidability	Article 492
Gift
Article 492 declares that a gift of future property is void.

dispossession,warranty	Article 494
Donor
Article 494 defines the conditions under which the donor warrants against dispossession of the gifted thing.

limitations,obstacles	Article 502
Revocation of Gift
Article 502 lists the obstacles that prevent revocation of a gift, such as inherent value increase, death of a party, and alienation.

legal notification,procedural requirement	Formal Summons to Pay
Third Party Holder
The Third Party Holder's declaration of abandonment must be entered in the margin of the transcription of the Formal Summons to Pay.

formation document,legal requirement	Partnership
Partnership Deed
The partnership deed is the written instrument required to establish a partnership, and must be executed in writing under penalty of nullity.

equal contributions,ownership presumption	Article 508
Partner
Article 508 presumes partners' contributions to be equal and to consist of ownership of property unless otherwise agreed.

defect warranty,liability	Article 495
Donor
Article 495 addresses the donor's liability for defects in the gifted thing, particularly when defects are intentionally hidden.

judicial authority,legal process	Court
Revocation of Gift
The court has the authority to permit revocation of a gift when the donee does not consent and the donor has reasonable grounds.

legal protection,rights preservation	Good Faith
Third Party Holder
A Third Party Holder in Good Faith is protected in rights acquired during the interval between the extinguishment and revival of a mortgage.

nullity,writing requirement	Article 507
Partnership Deed
Article 507 requires the partnership deed to be in writing, prescribing nullity for non-compliance and limiting the effect of nullity between partners.

corporate status,legal personality	Juristic Person
Partnership
A partnership is deemed a juristic person upon constitution, acquiring legal personality enforceable against third parties after publication formalities.

interest liability,unpaid contribution	Article 510
Partner
Article 510 makes a partner liable for interest on unpaid monetary contributions from the due date, plus compensation for any loss.

governing provisions,legal reference	Article 491
Articles 466 and 467
Article 491 directs that gifts of specific things not belonging to the donor are governed by the provisions of Articles 466 and 467.

legal prohibition,voidability	Article 492
Future Property
Article 492 declares that a gift of future property is void and has no legal effect.

consent,restitution	Donee
Revocation of Gift
The donee may consent to revocation or contest it, and is liable for restitution of fruits from the date of agreement or legal proceedings.

legal protection,warranty	Article 494
Dispossession
Article 494 governs the donor's warranty obligations against dispossession of the gifted thing, including liability for intentional concealment and limits based on valuable consideration.

legal derivation,property transfer	Judgment of Adjudication
Third Party Holder
When a person other than the Third Party Holder acquires the property at auction, that person's right is derived from the Third Party Holder by virtue of the Judgment of Adjudication.

eligibility requirement,legal condition	Creditor
Good Faith
A Creditor must be in Good Faith to obtain a Judgment Charge over the Debtor's immovable property.

contractual elements,legal definition	Article 505
Partnership
Article 505 defines partnership as a contract involving contributions of property or services for sharing profits or losses.

legal recognition,third parties	Article 506
Juristic Person
Article 506 establishes that a partnership acquires juristic personality upon constitution, with publication formalities required for recognition by third parties.

fault standard,liability limitation	Article 496
Donor
Article 496 limits the donor's liability exclusively to intentional acts or gross negligence, excluding liability for minor faults.

property contribution,warranty provisions	Article 511
Partner
Article 511 applies sale or lease warranty provisions to a partner's property contributions, depending on whether ownership or use is contributed.

financial obligation,revocation grounds	Alimony
Article 501
Article 501 establishes that the donor's inability to meet a legally binding alimony obligation constitutes a reasonable ground for revocation of a gift.

marital gift,revocation obstacle	Article 502
Spouse
Article 502 provides that a gift made by one spouse to another cannot be revoked, even after the dissolution of the marriage.

restitution,revocation effects	Article 503
Fruits
Article 503 provides that upon revocation, the donee is liable for restitution of fruits only from the date of agreement on revocation or commencement of legal proceedings.

compensation,equitable remedy	Donee
Judge
The judge awards equitable compensation to the donee for prejudice suffered when the donor intentionally concealed the cause of dispossession.

legal right,substitution	Article 494
Subrogation
Article 494 establishes that in a case of dispossession, the donee is subrogated into the rights and actions of the donor.

repeal,replacement	Egyptian Civil Code
National Courts
The Egyptian Civil Code repealed the previous civil law applied before National Courts and replaced it with a new comprehensive civil code.

external relationship,legal standing	Partnership
Third Party
Third parties interact with the partnership and may invoke its juristic personality even when publication formalities have not been completed, as provided under Article 506.

profit accounting,service contribution	Article 512
Partner
Article 512 requires a partner contributing services to perform those services and account for resulting profits, without obligating transfer of patents.

property contribution,warranty provisions	Article 511
Usufruct
Article 511 applies the provisions governing sale warranties to a partner's contribution consisting of a usufruct or other real right.

legal governance,personal status	Egypt
Legal Capacity
Legal capacity provisions apply to all persons who fulfill the conditions set by Egyptian legislative provisions.

judicial decision-making,legal hierarchy	Custom
Judge
The Judge applies custom as a source of law when no applicable legislative provision exists.

legal period,time calculation	Gregorian Calendar
Prescription
Prescription periods are calculated according to the Gregorian Calendar unless expressly provided otherwise by law.

legal substitution,rights transfer	Donee
Subrogation
Through subrogation, the donee acquires the rights and actions of the donor in cases of dispossession of the gifted thing.

repeal,replacement	Egyptian Civil Code
Mixed Courts
The Egyptian Civil Code repealed the previous civil law applied before Mixed Courts and replaced it with a new comprehensive civil code.

legal recognition,publication formalities	Article 506
Third Party
Article 506 requires completion of publication formalities before a partnership's juristic personality can be invoked against third parties, while allowing third parties to invoke it even without such formalities.

debt contribution,obligation,recovery obligation	Article 513
Partner
Article 513 governs a Partner whose contribution consists of debts due by third parties, requiring recovery of those debts to extinguish his obligation to the Partnership.<SEP>Article 513 states that a partner contributing debts due by third parties is only discharged upon recovery of those debts and is liable for damages if unpaid at maturity.

legal governance,territorial application	Egypt
Marriage
If one spouse is Egyptian at the time of marriage, Egyptian law alone applies to the marriage's conditions and effects.

judicial decision-making,legal hierarchy	Islamic Sharia
Judge
The Judge applies principles of Islamic Sharia when neither legislative provisions nor custom are available.

execution,implementation	Egyptian Civil Code
Minister of Justice
The Minister of Justice is tasked with executing and implementing the Egyptian Civil Code starting from October 15, 1949.

post-mortem disposition,succession law	Inheritance
Will
Wills are a form of post-mortem disposition governed by the national law of the testator at the time of death, with special rules for the form of the will.

dischargeable,management	Non-Partner Manager
Partnership
A Non-Partner Manager may manage the Partnership but, unlike a managing partner appointed under the Partnership Deed, may be discharged from his post at any time.

continuation,succession	Article 528
Heirs
Article 528 permits the Partnership to continue with the Heirs of a deceased partner by agreement, with the Heirs entitled to the deceased partner's share valued at the date of the triggering event.

abstention,duty of care,fiduciary duty	Article 521
Partner
Article 521 obliges each Partner to abstain from activities prejudicial to the Partnership and to exercise the same standard of care as for his own interests, with a higher standard for remunerated managers.

lawful act,regulatory impact	Government Authority
Leased Property
Lawful acts by a government authority may appreciably diminish the enjoyment of the leased property, entitling the lessee to remedies.

legal obligation,protection	Lessor
Warranty Against Disturbance
The lessor is obligated to warrant the lessee against disturbances from the lessor, the lessor's servants, other lessees, or successors in title.

capital loss,dissolution	Article 527
Partnership
Article 527 provides that the Partnership ends upon total or substantial loss of its capital, and is dissolved if a specific thing pledged as contribution perishes before delivery.

appointment,discharge	Article 516

Article 516 provides that Non-Partner Managers are always dischargeable from their management post, unlike managing partners appointed by the Partnership Deed.

general usage,maintenance obligation	Lessee

The lessee is bound to carry out lessee's repairs in accordance with general usage, unless otherwise agreed in the lease.

interest entitlement,interest liability	Article 522

Article 522 makes a Partner liable for interest on Partnership money taken or retained and entitles a Partner to interest on private funds advanced to the Partnership in good faith.

interference,rights claim,trespass	Leased Property

A third party may claim rights over the leased property or commit trespass, triggering the lessee's obligation to notify the lessor and the right to take legal action.

legal obligation,property condition	Lessor
Warranty Against Defects
The lessor warrants the leased property against defects that prevent or appreciably diminish enjoyment, except for defects customarily tolerated or known to the lessee.

damage responsibility,liability	Fire
Lessee
The lessee is responsible for fire damage to the leased property unless the cause is proven not imputable to the lessee; when multiple lessees occupy the building, responsibility is proportional to the part occupied unless the fire originated in one specific lessee's part.

apportionment,insolvency	Article 524

co-tenancy,competition,priority	Leased Property

When several lessees rent the same property, the one who without fraud first enters into possession has preference; if none has grounds for preference, each may only claim damages for rights not enjoyed.

retention,security right	Lessor

security obligation,stocking requirement	Lessee

contribution,proportional sharing	Partner
Partnership Capital
A Partner's share in profits and losses of the Partnership is proportional to his contribution to the Partnership Capital when the Partnership Deed does not fix respective shares.

administration,management	Administrator
Estate
The Administrator is responsible for managing, inventorying, and administering the Estate, including recovering claims, paying debts, and distributing remaining assets.

compensation,liability	Damages
Lessor
The lessor is liable to pay damages to the lessee for losses caused by defects, disturbances, or government acts imputable to the lessor.

permission requirement,restriction	Alteration
Lessee
The lessee may not make alterations to the leased property without the lessor's permission unless no damage is occasioned to the lessor; unauthorized alterations may compel reinstatement and compensation.

authorization,reporting	Administrator
Court
The Administrator files the inventory with the Court, seeks Court authorization for debt payments, and acts under Court authority in estate matters.

agency,responsibility	Lessor
Servants of the Lessor
The lessor is responsible for the acts of the lessor's servants that cause disturbance or damage to the lessee's enjoyment of the property.

obligation,return of property	Lessee

The lessee is bound upon expiration of the lease to return the leased property; unlawful retention results in compensation liability based on the rental value and harm to the lessor.

filing,preparation	Administrator

The Administrator prepares and files the Inventory with the Registry of the Court within four months of appointment, recording all claims and debts of the estate.

certification,dispute resolution	Court
Heirs
The Court issues inheritance certificates to Heirs upon production of an Elam Charei, resolves disputes over inventory and division, and orders the sale or allocation of family papers and sentimental articles.

succession,warranty coverage	Lessor
Successor in Title
The lessor warrants the lessee against lawful claims made by any successor in title of the lessor.

debt claims,secured interests	Creditors
Estate
Creditors hold claims against the Estate for unpaid debts and are entitled to payment from estate assets, with or without security on estate property.

preference,priority	Good Faith
Lessee
A lessee who in good faith first enters into possession of the leased property or transcribes the lease before another lessee takes possession will have preference over competing lessees.

inheritance,succession	Deceased
Heirs
Heirs are the legal successors of the Deceased, entitled to inherit property and obligated to report known debts and claims of the estate.

dispute adjudication,oversight	Court
Inventory
The Court investigates disputes regarding the accuracy of the Inventory and admits or rejects claims by order within thirty days of the inventory filing notice.

contractual party,obligations	Agreement of Lease
Lessor
The lessor is a party to the agreement of lease, bound by its terms including warranties and obligations regarding the leased property.

asset liquidation,forced sale	Estate
Public Auction
Movable and immovable property of the Estate is sold by Public Auction in accordance with rules for forced sales, unless all heirs agree to an alternative method.

compliance,general usage	Custom
Lessee
In the absence of express agreement, the lessee must comply with local custom regarding rent payment times, tolerated defects, and lessee's repairs, as established by the practice of the place where the property is situated.

delivery,distribution	Administrator
Heirs
The Administrator delivers estate property to the Heirs, proceeds with amicable or judicial division, and provides interim delivery of items not needed for winding up the estate.

protection,security arrangement	Court
Creditors
The Court arranges adequate security for Creditors on estate property and ensures their approval is obtained for non-auction sales when the estate is insolvent.

disturbance,warranty coverage	Lessor
Other Lessee
The lessor warrants the primary lessee against disturbances or damage based on lawful claims by any other lessee, extending the lessor's warranty beyond the lessor's own acts.

origin,ownership	Deceased
Estate
The Estate comprises all property, assets, rights, and liabilities that belonged to the Deceased at the time of death.

contractual party,obligations	Agreement of Lease
Lessee
The lessee is a party to the agreement of lease, deriving rights such as enjoyment of the property and obligations such as rent payment and proper use.

bequest,testamentary division	Heirs
Will
A Will may divide the property of the estate among Heirs, setting out each heir's share, with any excess over the hereditary share deemed a legacy.

debt settlement,payment	Administrator

The Administrator discharges estate debts to Creditors using estate funds, proceeds from asset sales, and suspends payments if the estate is insolvent.

certification prerequisite,documentation	Court

An heir must produce an Elam Charei to the Court in order to obtain a certificate establishing rights in the inheritance and the extent of the heir's share.

fraudulent concealment,void agreement	Fraud
Lessor
If the lessor fraudulently conceals the cause of a warranty against disturbance or defects, any agreement excluding or limiting such warranty is void.

dispute,notification	Interested Party
Inventory
An Interested Party must be informed of the filing of the Inventory by registered letter and may dispute its accuracy by petition to the Court within thirty days.

legal compliance,procedural framework	Forced Sales
Public Auction
Public Auction of estate property is conducted in accordance with the manner and delays laid down for Forced Sales.

authorship,testamentary disposition	Deceased
Will
The Will is a testamentary disposition made by the Deceased, dividing estate property among heirs and becoming irrevocable upon the death of the testator.

extinguishment,legal effect	Extinctive Prescription

Extinctive Prescription extinguishes the Obligation after the applicable period has elapsed, leaving only a natural obligation upon the debtor.

employment,valuation assistance	Administrator

The Administrator may employ an Expert for the preparation of the inventory and the estimation of the value of the estate property.

legal recourse,procedural governance	Code Of Procedure
Court
The Code of Procedure governs the recourse available against Court orders admitting claims related to inventory disputes.

bidding rights,participation	Heirs

Heirs are always entitled to take part in the Public Auction of estate movable and immovable property.

financial obligation,owed to	State

Taxes and Dues are financial obligations owed to the State, with a specific three-year prescription period.

defense,legal protection	Debtor
Extinctive Prescription
Extinctive Prescription benefits the Debtor by extinguishing obligations, but the Debtor cannot renounce it before acquiring the right to invoke it.

extension request,judicial approval	Administrator
Judge
The Administrator may apply to the Judge for an extension of time for filing the inventory if justified by circumstances.

allocation,dispute resolution	Court

The Court orders either the sale or allocation of Family Papers to one of the heirs, with or without deduction from the heir's share, in the absence of agreement.

fraudulent appropriation,penalty	Heirs

An Heir who fraudulently appropriates a part of the assets of the estate is liable to the penalties for Misappropriation under Article 889.

binding obligation,transfer	Sale Contract
Vendor
The Sale Contract binds the Vendor to transfer ownership of a thing or propriety right to the Purchaser.

claim restriction,limitation	Creditor

Extinctive Prescription limits the Creditor's ability to enforce claims after the prescribed period has elapsed.

execution,testamentary compliance	Administrator
Will
The Administrator executes the provisions of the Will after the settlement of all estate debts.

allocation,economic unity preservation	Agricultural Industrial Or Commercial Enterprise

The Court ensures that an Agricultural, Industrial or Commercial Enterprise constituting a distinct economic unity is allotted as a whole to the most capable heir.

legal effect,residual duty	Debtor

A Natural Obligation remains upon the Debtor even after the original legal obligation has been extinguished by prescription.

acquisition,consideration	Purchaser
Sale Contract
The Sale Contract entitles the Purchaser to acquire ownership of a thing in consideration of a price in money.

five-year term,prescription period	Extinctive Prescription
Periodic Payments
Periodic Payments are subject to a five-year extinctive prescription period, even if the debt is admitted by the debtor.

payment,testamentary charges	Administrator
Legacies
The Administrator proceeds with the payment of Legacies and other charges after the discharge of the debts of the estate.

judicial direction,procedural requirement	Judge
Oath of Payment
The Judge directs the Oath of Payment of his own accord in cases where the one-year prescription is invoked.

contract type,variation	Sale Contract
Sale by Sample
Sale by Sample is a specific form of Sale Contract requiring the thing sold to conform to the sample provided.

documentation,prescription extension	Professional Remuneration

If a right to Professional Remuneration is established by a Written Document, its prescription period extends to fifteen years.

security,tacit acknowledgment	Debtor
Pledge
A Debtor who leaves a Pledge with the creditor as security for a debt is deemed to have tacitly acknowledged the debt.

procedural condition,proof	Oath of Payment
One-Year Prescription Rights
The Oath of Payment is a mandatory procedural condition for any person invoking the One-Year Prescription Rights.

contractual misconduct,deception	Fraud
Vendor
Fraud may be committed by the Vendor in a sale contract by misrepresenting the thing sold to the Purchaser.

conditional sale,contract type	Sale Contract
Sale upon Trial
Sale upon Trial is a specific form of Sale Contract deemed subject to a suspensive condition of acceptance by the purchaser.

five-year term,prescription period	Extinctive Prescription
Professional Remuneration
Professional Remuneration claims are subject to a five-year extinctive prescription period from the time prestations were made.

acknowledgment,interruption trigger	Pledge
Prescription Interruption
A Pledge left with the creditor constitutes a tacit acknowledgment that triggers Prescription Interruption.

procedural duty,successor obligation	Heirs and Guardians
Oath of Payment
Heirs and Guardians of a deceased debtor may be required to take the Oath of Payment, declaring whether they know of the debt or its payment.

annulment,legal remedy	Fraud
Purchaser
Fraud proven against the Vendor entitles the Purchaser to claim annulment of the sale even when the contract states the Purchaser is acquainted with the thing sold.

conditional sale,contract type	Sale Contract
Sale Subject to Tasting
Sale Subject to Tasting is a specific form of Sale Contract where the sale is only concluded upon the purchaser's declaration of acceptance.

prescription period,three-year term	Extinctive Prescription
Taxes and Dues
Taxes and Dues are subject to a three-year extinctive prescription period running from the end of the year for which they are due.

equality,legal obligation,service provision	Concessionaire of Public Utility Service
Consumer
The Concessionaire of Public Utility Service is bound to observe strict equality between consumers in the provision of services and rates charged.

legal succession,representation	Debtor
Heirs and Guardians
Heirs and Guardians succeed the Debtor's position in relation to the oath requirement upon the Debtor's death.

Article 670 enshrines the Principle of Equality requiring the concessionaire to treat consumers equally in services and rates.

liability exemption,unforeseeable event	Article 673

Article 673 allows the concessionaire to repudiate responsibility for service interruptions by proving they were caused by force majeure or fortuitous events.

Sale Contract
Book II: Specific Contracts governs the Sale Contract and other named contracts within the civil code.

Article 674 provides the legal definition of a Contract of Service as an agreement where one party works under the control of another for remuneration.

The Concessionaire of Public Utility Service must apply the rates laid down by the Public Authority, which have force of law.

employment relationship,remuneration,supervision	Employer

The Worker undertakes to perform work under the supervision or control of the Employer in exchange for remuneration under a contract of service.

legal right,waiver	Debtor

fortuitous event,liability exemption	Article 673

contract scope,legal applicability	Article 676

Article 676 extends contract of service provisions to apply to the relationship between employers and canvassers.

consumer protection,rate correction	Article 672
Consumer
Article 672 protects the Consumer by entitling recovery of excess payments due to rate irregularities or mistakes.

agency,commission,supervision	Commercial Representative

legal protection,salary components	Article 683

contract duration,termination rights	Article 678

Article 678 governs the permissible durations of a Contract of Service and the worker's right to terminate long-term contracts without compensation.

agency,commission,supervision	Commercial Traveller

The Commercial Traveller works under employer supervision and retains post-employment commission rights on orders resulting from prior efforts.

liability exemption,unforeseeable event	Article 673

Article 673 permits the concessionaire to repudiate responsibility for service interruptions caused by a fortuitous event that could not have been foreseen or avoided by vigilant management.

salary determination,tips	Article 684
Worker
Article 684 provides that tips may form part of the Worker's salary in certain industries when subject to regulation or collected in a common fund.

contract renewal,fixed-term termination	Article 679

Article 679 provides that a fixed-term Contract of Service terminates automatically upon expiration and is deemed renewed indefinitely if performance continues.

anti-discrimination,legal protection	Article 670

equity,judicial authority,salary determination	Article 682

agency,contract of service,supervision	Assurance Agent

The Assurance Agent works under the orders and supervision of the Employer and is subject to contract of service provisions even if remunerated on commission.

legal distinction,liability exemption	Force Majeure

A Fortuitous Event is distinguished from Force Majeure as a separate legal ground for the concessionaire to repudiate responsibility for abnormal service interruptions.

performance duties,worker obligations	Article 685
Worker
Article 685 imposes on the Worker the obligation to perform work personally with reasonable care and to obey lawful employer orders.

industry custom,salary component	Article 684
Tips

form requirements,legal formalities	Article 677

Article 677 establishes that a Contract of Service does not require any special form unless law or administrative regulations provide otherwise.

creditor rights,security	Contract Of Pledge

extension,fifteen-year term	Extinctive Prescription

contract scope,legal applicability	Article 676
Assurance Agent
Article 676 extends contract of service provisions to the relationship between masters and assurance agents.

presumption of remuneration,professional services	Article 681

authority,lawful orders,worker obligations	Article 685
Employer
Article 685 obliges the Worker to obey the Employer's orders related to the agreed work provided such orders do not violate the contract, law, or public morals.

contract termination,implied renewal,specific work	Article 680
Contract of Service
Article 680 provides that a Contract of Service for specific work terminates upon completion and may be impliedly renewed if the work is renewable by nature and performance continues.
