legal mechanism,substitution	Delegation
Novation
Delegation constitutes novation by change of debtor when the parties agree to substitute a new obligation for the original obligation.

consent,legal provision	Article 358
Suretyship
Article 358 requires consent of sureties and co-debtors for transferring suretyship to the new obligation.

legal provision,validity	Article 353
Novation
Article 353 establishes the conditions under which novation is valid, requiring both obligations to be free from nullity.

liberation,substitution	Debtor
Delegation
Delegation liberates the original debtor from the obligation to the creditor, provided the new debtor's obligation is valid and the new debtor is not insolvent.

definition,legal provision	Article 370
Merger
Article 370 defines merger and its effects on the extinction and potential revival of debt.

legal provision,voluntary release	Article 371
Release Of Obligation
Article 371 provides the rules for voluntary release of the debtor by the creditor.

legal provision,presumption	Article 354
Novation
Article 354 provides that novation is not presumed and must be expressly agreed or clearly inferred from circumstances.

payment,undertaking	Delegation
Third Party
In delegation, a third party undertakes to pay the creditor in the debtor's stead, with the creditor's acceptance.

debt extinguishment,right	Compensation (Set Off)
Debtor
The debtor has the right to invoke compensation to set off mutual debts with the creditor.

impossibility,legal provision	Article 373
Impossibility Of Performance
Article 373 establishes impossibility of performance as a ground for extinguishing obligations.

legal provision,prescription period	Article 374
Extinctive Prescription
Article 374 sets the general fifteen-year term for extinctive prescription.

effects,legal provision	Article 356
Novation
Article 356 defines the effects of novation on the original obligation, its accessories, and associated securities.

definition,legal provision	Article 359
Delegation
Article 359 defines delegation and its requirements.

extinction,unification	Debtor
Merger
Merger occurs when the qualities of creditor and debtor in the same debt unite in the same person, extinguishing the debt.

extinguishment,mutual debt	Compensation (Set Off)
Creditor
Compensation extinguishes both debts between the debtor and creditor to the extent of the smaller debt.

legal provision,periodic rights	Article 375
Extinctive Prescription
Article 375 prescribes a five-year prescription period for periodic rights such as rent, interest, wages, and pensions.

assignment rules,legal provision	Article 368
Assignment Of Debt
Article 368 governs the effect of assignment of debt on the debtor's right to set up compensation, distinguishing between consented and merely notified assignments.

legal provision,novation by delegation	Article 360
Delegation
Article 360 provides that delegation may constitute novation by change of debtor when parties agree to substitute obligations.

discharge,liberation	Debtor
Release Of Obligation
Release of obligation liberates the debtor upon the debtor becoming aware of the release, unless the debtor refuses.

limitation,protection	Compensation (Set Off)
Third Party
Compensation cannot take place to the detriment of rights acquired by third parties, including attaching creditors.

governing rules,legal provision	Article 372
Gift
Article 372 states that the substantive rules governing gifts apply to the release of an obligation.

assignment,transfer	Assignment Of Debt
Creditor
The creditor assigns the creditor's right to a third party through assignment of debt.

burden of proof,extinction	Debtor
Impossibility Of Performance
Impossibility of performance extinguishes the obligation if the debtor proves that performance became impossible due to causes beyond the debtor's control.

new debtor,redress	Delegation
Right Of Recourse
The right of recourse arises in the context of delegation when the new debtor's obligation towards the original debtor is void or contestable.

legal provision,right of compensation	Article 362
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 362 grants the debtor the right to compensation of mutual debts under specified conditions.

periodic payments,time limitation	Extinctive Prescription
Periodic Rights
Periodic rights are subject to a shortened five-year extinctive prescription period under Article 375.

governing rules,legal framework	Gift
Release Of Obligation
The substantive rules governing gifts apply to the release of an obligation as provided by Article 372.

assignee,transfer	Assignment Of Debt
Third Party
A third party becomes the assignee of the debt through assignment by the creditor.

element,formation	Consent
Contract
Consent through the exchange of concordant intentions is a fundamental element required for the creation of a contract.

exceptions,legal provision	Article 364
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 364 enumerates the exceptions where compensation does not apply.

initiation,proposal	Offer
Offeror
The offeror is the person who initiates an offer in the contract formation process.

ownership,public utility	Public Domain
State
The public domain includes immovable and movable property owned by the State and allocated for public utility purposes.

consent,notification	Assignment Of Debt
Debtor
The debtor's right to compensation is affected by assignment of debt depending on whether the debtor consented without reserve or merely received notification.

legal provision,place of payment	Article 363
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 363 permits compensation even when the places of payment of the two debts differ, provided the debtor compensates the creditor for any resulting loss.

agency,representation	Principal
Representative
A representative acts on behalf of a principal, and rights and obligations from contracts concluded within authority are binding upon the principal.

formation,proposal	Contract
Offer
An offer is a necessary component of contract formation, made by an offeror to another party.

ownership,public utility	Public Domain
Public Juristic Persons
The public domain includes immovable and movable property owned by public juristic persons and allocated for public utility purposes.

incapacity,voidness	Legal Capacity
Minor Lacking Discretion
A minor lacking discretion has no legal capacity to dispose of property, and all such acts are deemed void.

extinguishment,invocation,legal provision	Article 365
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 365 provides that compensation takes place only when invoked by the interested party, extinguishes both debts to the extent of the smaller amount, and cannot be renounced before the right arises.

instruction-based,type of	Mandatory
Representative
A mandatory is a specific type of representative who acts in accordance with the principal's precise instructions.

imposition,standard conditions	Contract Of Adhesion
Offeror
In a contract of adhesion, the offeror draws up standard conditions that are not subject to discussion by the accepting party.

agreement,formation	Acceptance
Contract
Acceptance of an offer completes the formation of a contract, provided it matches the offer without restriction or modification.

limited capacity,voidability	Discerning Minor
Legal Capacity
A discerning minor has limited legal capacity: purely beneficial acts are valid, harmful acts are void, and mixed acts are voidable for the minor's benefit.

legal provision,prescription interaction	Article 366
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 366 allows compensation to proceed even after the prescription period has expired for a debt, provided the period had not expired when compensation first became possible.

agency,formation	Contract
Representative
A representative may conclude a contract on behalf of a principal within the limits of his authority.

agreement,response	Acceptance
Offer
Acceptance is the response to an offer; if acceptance goes beyond, restricts, or modifies the offer, it is deemed a rejection comprising a new offer.

allocation,purpose	Public Domain
Public Utility
Property becomes part of the public domain when allocated for public utility purposes, and loses this status when the allocation for public utility ceases.

legal provision,third party protection	Article 367
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 367 prohibits compensation to the detriment of rights acquired by third parties, including when a third party has seized property held by the debtor for the creditor.

interaction,legal provision	Article 366
Extinctive Prescription
Article 366 governs the interaction between extinctive prescription and compensation, allowing compensation if the prescription period had not expired when compensation became possible.

enforcement,substitution	Judgment
Promise To Contract
When a party refuses to honor a promise to contract and legal proceedings enforce the promise, a final judgment substitutes for and replaces the contract itself.

legal validity,prerequisite,validity	Contract
Legal Capacity
Legal capacity is a prerequisite for a person to validly conclude a contract.

conflict of interest,prohibition	Representative
Self-Dealing
A representative is prohibited from contracting with himself in the name of the principal without authorization, to prevent conflicts of interest.

form of acceptance,legal equivalence	Acceptance
Silence As Acceptance
Silence or failure to reply constitutes a form of acceptance in specific circumstances, such as when the offer relates to existing dealings or is solely in the offeree's interest.

legal provision,securities,waiver	Article 369
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 369 provides that a debtor who paid despite having a right to compensation cannot invoke securities to the prejudice of third parties unless unaware of that right.

equivalence,legal framework	Obligations
Personal Rights
Obligations and personal rights are treated as equivalent concepts in the civil law framework, both referring to legal duties and corresponding rights between persons.

guarantee,withdrawal right	Contract
Earnest Money
Earnest money is paid at the time of contract conclusion and indicates the right of either party to withdraw, subject to forfeiture or double repayment.

collaboration,legal liability,shared privilege,warranty obligation	Architect
Contractor
Both the Architect and the Contractor are bound by warranty obligations for the works; any clause tending to exclude or restrict this warranty is void.<SEP>Contractors and architects share the same privilege over buildings or other works for which they have been entrusted with erection, reconstruction, repair, or maintenance.

authorization,ratification	Principal
Self-Dealing
A principal may authorize or subsequently ratify a contract where the representative engaged in self-dealing, overriding the general prohibition.

disclosure failure,third party	Representative
Undisclosed Representation
When a representative fails to disclose representative status at the time of contracting, the contract's effect on the principal depends on the third party's knowledge or indifference.

assignment limitation,legal provision	Article 368
Compensation (Set Off)
Article 368 limits the debtor's right to compensation after consenting to assignment of debt without reserve, while preserving it when the debtor has only been notified.

direct right of action,payment claim	Master
Sub-contractor
Sub-contractors and Workmen have a direct right of action against the Master to the extent of sums due by the Master to the main Contractor at the time the action is commenced.

future obligation,prerequisite	Contract
Promise To Contract
A promise to contract is an agreement to enter into a contract in the future, requiring all essential points and timeframe to be specified to be binding.

binding effect,knowledge	Principal
Undisclosed Representation
The principal is only bound by or benefits from a contract involving undisclosed representation if the third party necessarily knew of the representation or was indifferent to the identity of the contracting party.

direct right of action,privilege and priority	Master
Workmen
Workmen working for a Contractor or Sub-contractor have direct rights of action against the Master and enjoy priority of payment over assignees of the Contractor.

conclusion,sale method	Contract
Public Auction
A public auction is a method of forming a contract of sale, concluded only when the final bid is accepted.

concession agreement,public utility management	Administrative Authority
Concessionaire
The Administrative Authority concludes a concession agreement with the Concessionaire entrusting the exploitation of a public utility service for a fixed period.

reversion,unawareness	Extinction Of Representation
Principal
When both the representative and the third party were unaware that the representation had ended, the effects of the contract revert to the principal or his successor in title.

contractual relationship,delivery and payment	Contractor
Master
The Contractor executes works and places them at the Master's disposal; the Master is obligated to take delivery and pay the price upon delivery unless custom or agreement provides otherwise.

adjudication,dispute resolution	Contract
Court
The court resolves disputes over details of contracts by applying the nature of the transaction, law, custom, and equity.

equality obligation,service provision	Concessionaire
Consumer
The Concessionaire is obligated to provide services to Consumers in a normal manner at specified rates, and when enjoying a monopoly must observe strict equality among all Consumers.

fees,professional services	Architect
Master
The Architect provides the Master with design plans, specifications, and supervision of work, and is entitled to separate fees for each; fees are fixed according to prevailing custom if not specified in the contract.

delegation of work,responsibility	Contractor
Sub-contractor
The Contractor may entrust the execution of all or part of the work to a Sub-contractor but remains responsible to the Master for the Sub-contractor's work.

expression of will,formation	Contract
Declaration Of Intention
A declaration of intention is the means by which parties express their concordant intentions to form a contract.

compensation obligation,termination rights	Contract For Work
Master
The Master may terminate the Contract for Work at any time before completion, provided compensation is paid to the Contractor for expenses, completed work, and lost profit.

equality obligation,exclusive right	Concessionaire
Monopoly
When the Concessionaire enjoys a Monopoly, whether de jure or de facto, the Concessionaire is bound to observe strict equality among all consumers in the provision of services and the collection of rates, and is prohibited from granting advantages to some consumers while refusing them to others.

employment,payment rights	Contractor
Workmen
Workmen are employed by the Contractor in the execution of work and have rights of action against the main Contractor and the Master for sums due to them.

classification,source	Contract
Sources Of Obligations
Contracts are identified as one of the sources from which obligations arise, forming Section I of Chapter I on sources of obligations.

rights and obligations,substitution	Preemptor
Purchaser
The Preemptor is substituted for the Purchaser in all rights and obligations vis-a-vis the Vendor upon exercising the right of preemption.

contract continuation,guarantee requirement	Contractor's Heirs
Master
If the Contractor's personal skill was not a consideration, the Contractor's Heirs may continue the Contract for Work if they offer sufficient guarantees; otherwise, the Master may resiliate the contract.

contract adjustment,judicial authority	Contract For Work
Court
The Court has authority to reduce compensation for lost profit, grant a price increase, or order the resiliation of the Contract for Work in cases of economic imbalance caused by exceptional unforeseen events.

legal right,property sale	Immovable Property
Preemption
Preemption applies specifically to the sale of immovable property, allowing qualified persons to substitute themselves in place of the purchaser.

legal obligation,prescription period	Contractor
Warranty
The Contractor is bound by warranty obligations; warranty actions are prescribed after three years from the date of destruction of the works or discovery of defects.

real rights,transfer mechanism	Contract
Ownership
Ownership of movables and immovables and other real rights are transferred by contract when the contract refers to an object belonging to the person disposing of it.

obligations,payment,rights	Preemptor
Vendor
The Preemptor assumes the Purchaser's obligations vis-a-vis the Vendor and cannot benefit from payment delays without the Vendor's consent.

dissolution by death,payment obligation	Contractor's Estate
Master
When the contract is dissolved by the death of the Contractor, the Master is bound to pay the Contractor's Estate the value of the work already done and expenses incurred, to the extent of the benefit derived, and may demand delivery of prepared materials and commenced plans against payment of a fair price.

property rights,right holder	Bare Owner
Preemption
The Bare Owner holds the right of preemption in case of a sale of all or part of the usufruct attached to the bare property.

cost overrun,notification obligation	Contractor
Unit Price Contract
Under a Unit Price Contract, the Contractor is bound to notify the Master forthwith of any anticipated considerable excess over the estimated price and forfeits the right to recover excess expenses if notification is not given.

data.tgt_id: Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
data.content:
legal governance,transfer requirements	Immovable Property
Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights
The Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights governs the transfer of ownership and other real rights over immovable property, requiring publication of relevant acts and instruments.

acquisition,acquisition on behalf of another,legal capacity,legal representation	Legal Representative
Possession
A legal representative may acquire possession on behalf of a person lacking discretion.<SEP>A Legal Representative may acquire possession on behalf of a person lacking discretion through legal representation.

adjudication,legal procedure	Court
Preemption
The Court handles actions in preemption, which must be introduced before the district court where the property is situated and enrolled on the Court list as a matter of urgency.

property rights,real rights	Movable Property
Ownership
Ownership of movable property is transferred by contract upon identification and may be subject to court-determined equity rules when mingled with other movables.

price excess,rescission right	Master
Unit Price Contract
Under a Unit Price Contract, the Master may rescind the contract and stop the work without delay if the estimated excess in price is considerable, provided the Master pays the Contractor for work done according to contract terms.

legal concept,preemption rights	Bare Owner
Hekr
In case of hekr, the Bare Owner holds preemption rights if the hekr right is sold, and the beneficiary of the hekr holds preemption rights if the bare property is sold.

right holder,usufruct rights	Preemption
Usufructuary
The Usufructuary holds the right of preemption in case of a sale of all or part of the bare property producing the usufruct.

indirect exercise,indirect possession,legal control,obligation to obey	Intermediary
Possession
An intermediary exercises possession in the name of the possessor and is obliged to follow instructions regarding such possession.<SEP>An Intermediary may exercise possession on behalf of the possessor provided the intermediary acts in the possessor's name and is bound to follow the possessor's instructions.

property rights,real rights	Immovable Property
Ownership
Ownership of immovable property is transferred by contract subject to the rules of the Law Regulating the Publication of Real Rights.

dispute resolution,equity	Court
Movable Property
The Court decides matters in accordance with the rules of equity when movables belonging to different owners become mingled and cannot be separated without deterioration.

preference rights,secured claims	Purchaser
Registered Creditors
Registered Creditors retain their rights of preference on the portion of the sale price of the property that reverts to the Purchaser, even after preemption is exercised.

authorization,modification approval	Lump Sum Contract
Master
Under a Lump Sum Contract, the Master may authorize modifications or additions to the plan and agree on a price for them with the Contractor; such agreement must be in writing unless the principal contract was verbal.

joint ownership,right holder	Co-Owner in Common
Preemption
The Co-Owner in Common holds the right of preemption when a part of the common property is sold to a third party.

acquisition,legal capacity	Person Lacking Discretion
Possession
A Person Lacking Discretion may acquire possession only through the intervention of a Legal Representative acting on their behalf.

notification,procedural requirement	Formal Summons
Vendor
A Formal Summons must be served by the Vendor or the Purchaser to the prospective preemptor to initiate the preemption notification period.

buildings,compensation,plantations	Immovable Property
Preemptor
The Preemptor is bound to compensate the Purchaser for buildings or plantations constructed on the Immovable Property before notification of preemption, and may request removal of those constructed after notification.

dispute resolution,equitable consideration	Court
Good Faith
The Court considers the Good Faith of each party when deciding matters related to mingled movables in accordance with the rules of equity.

governed by,legal provision	Article 176
Liability Arising from Things
Article 176 is one of the legal provisions governing liability arising from things, specifically addressing liability for harm caused by animals.

loss bearing,supply responsibility	Master
Materials
The Master bears the loss of materials supplied by the Master when works are destroyed by a fortuitous event before delivery, or when destruction is caused by the Master's fault or a defect in materials supplied by the Master.

no increase claim,price limitation	Contractor
Lump Sum Contract
Under a Lump Sum Contract, the Contractor has no claim to an increase in price due to modifications, additions, or rises in material and labor costs, even if such increases render performance onerous.

adjoining property,right holder	Neighboring Owner
Preemption
The Neighboring Owner holds the right of preemption in cases involving buildings, building land, rights of servitude, or land adjoining on two sides.

governed by,legal provision	Article 179
Enrichment Without Just Cause
Article 179 is the primary legal provision establishing the principle of enrichment without just cause and the obligation to compensate.

governed by,legal provision	Article 181
Payment Not Due
Article 181 establishes the core principle that undue payments must be returned and exceptions to this rule.

governed by,legal provision	Article 177
Liability Arising from Things
Article 177 is one of the legal provisions governing liability arising from things, specifically addressing liability for damage caused by building collapse.

indemnification,loss bearing	Contractor
Materials
The Contractor bears the loss of materials supplied by the Contractor when works are destroyed by a fortuitous event before delivery, and must indemnify the Master for materials supplied by the Master if destruction or deterioration is caused by the Contractor's fault.

exclusion,prohibition	Preemption
Wakf
A Wakf is explicitly prohibited from exercising the right of preemption under Article 939.

preemption eligibility,property rights	Neighboring Owner
Right of Servitude
The existence of a Right of Servitude over neighboring land or in favor of neighboring land is one of the conditions that qualifies the Neighboring Owner to exercise the right of preemption.

governed by,legal provision	Article 180
Enrichment Without Just Cause
Article 180 sets the prescription periods for claims arising from enrichment without just cause.

governed by,legal provision	Article 188
Voluntary Agency
Article 188 defines voluntary agency as the voluntary assumption of management of another's urgent business.

governed by,legal provision	Article 182
Payment Not Due
Article 182 allows recovery of payments made for obligations whose cause had not materialized or had ceased to exist.

governed by,legal provision	Article 178
Liability Arising from Things
Article 178 is one of the legal provisions governing liability arising from things, specifically addressing liability for damage caused by things requiring special care or machines.

contract dissolution,death or impossibility	Contract For Work
Contractor
The Contract for Work is dissolved upon the death of the Contractor if personal skill was a factor, or if performance of the work becomes impossible.

exclusion,sale method	Preemption
Public Auction
Preemption cannot be exercised if the sale of the immovable property is conducted by Public Auction in accordance with legally prescribed procedures.

governed by,legal provision	Article 189
Voluntary Agency
Article 189 extends voluntary agency to cases where the agent manages connected businesses.

governed by,legal provision	Article 183
Payment Not Due
Article 183 governs restitution of premature payments made by a payor unaware that the obligation was not yet due.

governed by,legal provision	Article 199
Effects of Obligations
Article 199 establishes the enforceability of obligations and the exception for natural obligations.

governed by,legal provision	Article 190
Voluntary Agency
Article 190 provides that rules of mandate apply upon ratification by the principal.

governed by,legal provision	Article 184
Payment Not Due
Article 184 limits restitution rights when a creditor in good faith has given up documents or security due to a third party's payment.

governed by,legal provision	Article 200
Effects of Obligations
Article 200 empowers the judge to determine natural obligations in the absence of legal provisions.

custody,distinction	Owner
Person in Charge of Animal
A person in charge of an animal may be different from the owner, yet still bears liability for harm caused by the animal.

governed by,legal provision	Article 191
Voluntary Agency
Article 191 imposes duties on the voluntary agent to continue work and inform the principal.

governed by,legal provision	Article 185
Payment Not Due
Article 185 distinguishes the obligations of good faith and bad faith recipients of undue payments.

judicial authorization,preventive measures	Court
Person in Charge of Building
An endangered person may obtain a court order to take preventive measures against building danger at the owner's cost if the owner fails to act.

governed by,legal provision	Article 201
Effects of Obligations
Article 201 prevents restitution of voluntary payments made to discharge a natural obligation.

duty of care,indemnification,reimbursement,representation	Principal
Voluntary Agent
The principal is bound to carry out obligations entered into by the voluntary agent, indemnify him, reimburse expenses with interest, and compensate for loss.<SEP>The voluntary agent manages the principal's urgent business and owes duties of care, continuation, and notification to the principal.

restitution,undue payment	Creditor
Payor
The payor who makes a payment not due may claim restitution from the creditor, subject to exceptions based on good faith and legal capacity.

governed by,legal provision	Article 192
Voluntary Agency
Article 192 sets the standard of care for voluntary agents and rules on delegation and joint liability.

contrasting states,legal standard	Bad Faith
Good Faith
Good faith and bad faith are contrasting legal states that determine the extent of a recipient's obligation to return undue payments and profits.

governed by,legal provision	Article 186
Payment Not Due
Article 186 limits the liability of recipients lacking legal capacity to the extent of their enrichment.

legal claim,time limitation	Prescription
Restitution
Claims for restitution are subject to prescription periods of three years from knowledge and fifteen years from when the right arose.

custody,distinction	Owner
Person in Charge of Building
A person in charge of a building may be different from the owner, yet still bears liability for damage caused by its collapse.

cause,enforceability,legal basis	Civil Obligation
Natural Obligation
A natural obligation may constitute a valid cause for a civil obligation.<SEP>A natural obligation is not enforceable but may serve as a valid cause for a civil obligation, which is enforceable against the debtor.

governed by,legal provision	Article 202
Effects of Obligations
Article 202 provides that a natural obligation may serve as valid cause for a civil obligation.

governed by,legal provision	Article 193
Voluntary Agency
Article 193 binds voluntary agents to the same obligations as mandataries regarding restitution and accounting.

judicial proceeding,trigger event	Article 185
Court
The filing of a claim in court triggers the obligation to restitute interest and profits from the date of the claim, even for a good faith recipient.

governed by,legal provision	Article 198
The Law
Article 198 is the sole provision under Section V (The Law), establishing that obligations arising directly from the law are governed by the legal provisions that created them.

governed by,legal provision	Article 187
Payment Not Due
Article 187 sets the prescription periods for restitution claims of payments unduly received.

delegation,responsibility	Delegate
Voluntary Agent
A voluntary agent who delegates the whole or part of the work to a third party is responsible for the acts of the delegate, without prejudice to the principal's direct remedy against the delegate.

capacity limitation,enrichment	Legal Capacity
Restitution
>A recipient lacking legal capacity is liable for restitution only to the extent of his enrichment from the undue payment.

determination,judicial discretion,legal authority,legal determination	Judge
Natural Obligation
The judge decides, in the absence of legal provision, whether a natural obligation exists.<SEP>The judge determines whether a natural obligation exists in the absence of a legal provision, provided it is not contrary to public policy.

governed by,legal provision	Article 194
Voluntary Agency
Article 194 addresses the obligations of heirs upon the death of a voluntary agent or principal.

exception,restitution right	Duress
Payor
A payor who made a payment under duress may claim restitution even if he knew he was not obligated to pay, as provided in Article 181.

custody,liability for harm	Animal
Person in Charge of Animal
The person in charge of an animal bears liability for any harm the animal causes, even if the animal strays or escapes.

custody,liability for collapse	Building
Person in Charge of Building
The person in charge of a building bears liability for damage caused by its collapse, even if partial, unless due to negligent maintenance, age, or defect.

analogous legal framework,ratification	Mandate
Voluntary Agent
The rules of mandate apply to a voluntary agent when the principal ratifies the agent's act, and the voluntary agent is bound by the same obligations as a mandatary regarding restitution and accounting.

liability for damage,supervision	Machine
Person in Charge of Things
The person in charge of a machine bears liability for damage caused by it, unless the damage was due to a cause beyond control.

exception,liability override	Legal Capacity
Unlawful Act
The limitation of liability based on lack of legal capacity does not apply when the liability of a voluntary agent results from an unlawful act.

compliance,constraint,legal limitation,validity constraint	Natural Obligation
Public Policy
No natural obligation can exist that is contrary to public policy.<SEP>A natural obligation cannot exist if it is contrary to public policy, as established in Article 200.

indivisibility,legal invalidity	Compromise
Compromise Nullity
A compromise is indivisible, meaning the nullity of one part involves the nullity of the whole contract, unless the parties agreed the parts are independent.

governed by,legal provision	Article 195
Voluntary Agency
Article 195 establishes the representative status of the voluntary agent and the compensation obligations of the principal.

granting authority,property rights	Lease
Usufructuary
A usufructuary may grant leases that end when the usufruct is extinguished unless ratified by the bare owner.

data.src_id: Chapter II: Contracts Relating to the Use of a Thing
data.content:
hierarchy,legal structure	Chapter II: Contracts Relating to the Use of a Thing
Section I: Leases
Section I on Leases is part of Chapter II covering contracts relating to the use of a thing.

inherited obligation,succession	Heirs
Voluntary Agent
Upon the death of a voluntary agent, his heirs are bound by the same obligations as those of a mandatary's heirs under Article 717.

consent requirement,lease authorization	Competent Authority
Right of Management
A person holding only a right of management must obtain the consent of the competent authority to enter into a lease exceeding three years.

damage claim,legal remedy	Compensation
Lessee
The lessee is entitled to claim compensation when the leased property is unfit for use, its usefulness is diminished, or the lessor fails to fulfill maintenance obligations.

legal effect,rights determination	Compromise
Declaratory Effect
A compromise has a declaratory effect on the rights it covers, meaning it establishes rather than creates rights, and this effect is limited exclusively to the disputed rights.<SEP>A compromise has a declaratory effect on the rights it covers, and this effect is limited specifically to litigious rights.

governed by,legal provision	Article 196
Voluntary Agency
Article 196 limits liability of legally incapable voluntary agents while maintaining the principal's full responsibility.

property ownership,ratification	Bare Owner
Usufructuary
A lease granted by a usufructuary requires ratification by the bare owner to survive beyond the extinguishment of the usufruct.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1144
Hotel Proprietor's Privilege
Article 1144 establishes the hotel proprietor's privilege over effects brought by a traveller to secure sums due for accommodation, food, and expenses.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1145
Vendor's Privilege Over Movable
Article 1145 establishes the vendor's privilege over movable property sold to secure the price and accessories due.

continued obligation,succession	Heirs
Principal
Upon the death of the principal, the voluntary agent remains bound by the same obligations to the heirs as he was to the deceased principal.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1146
Co-partitioner's Privilege Over Movable
Article 1146 establishes the co-partitioner's privilege over partitioned movables for remedies and repayment of differences.

duration restriction,legal limitation	Lease
Right of Management
A person holding only a right of management cannot enter into a lease exceeding three years without the consent of the competent authority.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1147
Vendor's Privilege Over Immovable
Article 1147 establishes the vendor's privilege over immovable property sold to secure the price and accessories due.

judicial authorization,repair enforcement	Court
Lessee
The lessee may seek authorization from the court to carry out repairs and deduct the costs from rent when the lessor delays performance of maintenance obligations.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1148
Contractor's And Architect's Privilege
Article 1148 establishes the contractor's and architect's privilege over buildings or works to secure sums due for construction, repair, or maintenance.

right extinguishment,strict interpretation	Compromise
Renunciation
Renunciation contained in a compromise must be strictly interpreted and applies only to rights that form the precise object of the dispute settled by the compromise.

establishment,legal provision	Article 1149
Co-partitioner's Privilege Over Immovable
Article 1149 establishes the co-partitioner's privilege over partitioned immovables for remedies and payment of differences.

governed by,legal provision	Article 197
